signals.topic: Plan Mode UI hangs after plan_mode_respond, making extension completely unresponsive
signals.summary: After using plan_mode_respond tool in Plan Mode, the interface completely hangs and becomes unresponsive. User must click 'cancel' to regain control. This happens on every single Plan Mode interaction, making it impossible to have normal conversations or submit bug reports.
signals.review_reason: 主流程完全阻断。用户无法进行任何 Plan Mode 交互，甚至连提交此 bug 报告本身都受影响（因为报告也是在 Plan Mode 中提交的）。界面 hang 是每次必现，直接导致所有对话流程中断，属于高优先级 UI 阻断问题。

source_issues.title: Plan Mode: Interface hangs after plan_mode_respond, prevents bug reporting and all conversation flow
source_issues.evidence: UI completely hangs on every Plan Mode interaction. User must click cancel to regain control. Blocks bug reporting and all conversation flow. Reported as happening on every single Plan Mode interaction without exception.

signals.topic: Extension host crash loop caused by terminal output capture failure and memory exhaustion
signals.summary: Cline extension crashes VS Code extension host after a few minutes of use, causing a restart loop. Terminal output capture fails 115+ times per session, creating a retry loop that consumes CPU and accumulates memory until the extension host crashes.
signals.review_reason: 主流程阻断 + 崩溃。扩展在 2-5 分钟内必然崩溃重启，导致扩展完全不可用。终端输出捕获失败每会话出现 115+ 次，触发重试循环导致内存耗尽，PendingMigrationError 加剧问题。用户被迫反复重启 VS Code，属于严重的主流程崩溃问题。

source_issues.title: [Bug] Extension host crash loop: terminal output capture failure + PendingMigrationError causing memory exhaustion
source_issues.evidence: Extension crashes after 2-5 minutes. 'Error while asking for command output' occurs 115+ times per session. Retry loop accumulates memory (terminal buffers not released). PendingMigrationError: 'navigator is now a global in nodejs'. Users must restart VS Code repeatedly. Related to issues #7624, #8778, #5289, #8580.

signals.topic: Cline freezes indefinitely in 'thinking' state after execute_command reads terminal output
signals.summary: After Cline runs a terminal command via execute_command and attempts to read/process its console output, it switches to a 'thinking' state and stalls indefinitely. The UI becomes completely unresponsive. Happened at least 4 times across separate task launches. Only recovery is restarting VS Code.
signals.review_reason: 主流程完全阻断。每次执行包含终端命令的任务时必然触发冻结，UI 完全无响应，用户无法中止任务或开始新任务，唯一恢复方式是重启 VS Code。虽然 count=1，但冻结严重程度（必现、4次独立复现、唯一恢复方式是重启）达到 P0 阈值。

source_issues.title: Cline freezes indefinitely in 'thinking' state after execute_command reads terminal output, making UI unresponsive
source_issues.evidence: UI becomes completely unresponsive after execute_command reads terminal output. User cannot abort task, send new message, or start new task. Happened at least 4 times across separate task launches. Only recovery option is restarting VS Code.

signals.topic: OpenAI o3/o1 reasoning models produce 400 Bad Request errors due to reasoning/tool-call sequence ordering violations
signals.summary: When using OpenAI reasoning models (o1, o3-mini, o3) via the Responses API, users encounter 400 errors indicating 'Missing reasoning item'. Root cause is that the toResponsesInput function emits function_call items before the text message item, breaking the strict adjacency requirement between reasoning and output items in the OpenAI Responses API protocol.
aliases: o3 o1 reasoning item ordering bug
signals.review_reason: This is an active open bug (issue #11994) that blocks users from using OpenAI's reasoning models (o1/o3/o3-mini) with tool calls. The root cause is a sequence ordering violation in the OpenAI Responses API protocol. Issue #11976 was closed with a partial fix but the ordering issue in toResponsesInput remains unresolved. Users of reasoning models experience frequent 400 errors that prevent them from using Continue effectively with these models.

source_issues.title: [Bug] OpenAI Responses API 400 Bad Request: 'Missing reasoning item' with Reasoning Models
source_issues.evidence: Open issue: 400 error 'Item msg_... was provided without its required reasoning item rs_...'. Root cause: toResponsesInput emits function_call items before text message item, violating OpenAI Responses API's strict proximity/pairing protocol between reasoning blocks and output items.

source_issues.title: [Bug] 500 Internal Server Error in OpenAI o1/o3-mini Reasoning API when using tools
source_issues.evidence: Closed issue with PR fix: 500/400 errors during tool execution with reasoning models. Root cause: sanitizeResponsesInput incorrectly stripped valid function_call_output items, creating orphan tool outputs that violated API requirements.

signals.topic: UI progressively slows down and becomes sluggish in long conversations even after context compression
signals.summary: The Continue chat UI becomes progressively slower as conversations grow in length, affecting chat loading, conversation switching, and settings navigation. The compress feature does not resolve the issue, indicating a UI state management problem unrelated to context window size.
aliases: UI performance degradation in long conversations
signals.review_reason: This is a confirmed user-facing UX degradation that blocks smooth interaction with the core chat workflow. The fact that compress does not fix it indicates a memory leak or UI state management bug, not a context size issue. The user must manually close old conversations to restore performance, which is a significant workflow disruption.

source_issues.title: UI becomes extremely slow in long conversations
source_issues.evidence: User reports progressive UI sluggishness in chat loading, conversation switching, and settings menu with 500k+ token conversations. The compress feature does not fix it, indicating UI state leak independent of context size.

signals.topic: multi_edit silently fails when user replies without Accept/Reject, causing cascading model failures
signals.summary: When a user replies in chat without clicking Accept or Reject on a multi_edit diff, the tool call resolves with empty output. The model receives no failure signal and proceeds assuming the edit was applied, leading to subsequent edit attempts using wrong old_string values and cascading failures.
aliases: multi_edit silent failure on chat reply
signals.review_reason: This is a core workflow failure. The multi_edit tool is a primary feature of Continue. When the user neither accepts nor rejects and instead continues the conversation, the model incorrectly assumes the edit was applied. This creates cascading failures in subsequent tool calls as the file state diverges from what the model expects. The issue is reproducible and directly undermines trust in the apply/edit workflow.

source_issues.title: Replying to chat without clicking Accept or Reject on `multi_edit` produces 'No tool output'
source_issues.evidence: Confirmed bug where replying to chat without accepting/rejecting a multi_edit diff causes empty tool output. The model receives no failure signal and continues as if the edit succeeded, causing subsequent multi_edit calls to fail due to old_string mismatch with actual file contents.

signals.topic: Model configuration pages on continue.dev redirect to authentication, blocking unauthenticated access to setup instructions
signals.summary: All model configuration pages on continue.dev (e.g., ollama model setup pages) now redirect to an authentication page. Users can no longer access recommended YAML configuration examples without logging in, preventing them from discovering how to configure models.
signals.review_reason: This directly blocks users from onboarding and discovering model configurations. Previously public documentation pages are now gated behind authentication, which is a regression that prevents new users from learning how to set up models. The user can briefly see the target page before being redirected, confirming the content exists but is inaccessible. This is a service-wide regression affecting all model config documentation.

source_issues.title: All model configuration pages (such as https://continue.dev/ollama/qwen2.5-coder-1.5b) redirect to an authentication page
source_issues.evidence: User explicitly reports being unable to access model configuration documentation on continue.dev and docs.continue.dev without authentication. Before the change, these pages were publicly accessible. User does not want to authenticate just to see model configuration.

signals.topic: Gemini provider does not pass custom headers configured in config.yaml to the API, causing API key authentication failures
signals.summary: The Gemini provider ignores custom headers (including x-api-key) configured via requestOptions.headers in config.yaml. The code hard-codes only two headers. This results in 400 Bad Request 'API key not valid' errors for enterprise users using API proxies or custom endpoints with different auth mechanisms.
aliases: gemini provider x-api-key header not forwarded
signals.review_reason: This breaks the Gemini integration for enterprise users with custom API proxies. The user has a legitimate API key configured via headers but the code never forwards it, causing authentication failure. This is not an edge case - it affects all users who need custom headers for their Gemini setup (e.g., via proxies, gateway auth, or regional endpoints). The fix requires only passing through user-configured headers alongside hard-coded ones.

source_issues.title: Provider gemini does not pass custom headers to gemini API
source_issues.evidence: User with a custom API proxy (example.com) configured x-api-key in requestOptions.headers but receives 400 'API key not valid' error from the Gemini API. Root cause identified in code: Gemini.ts line 487 only sends hard-coded headers and ignores user-configured ones. The 400 error is caused by the correct API key not being forwarded.

signals.topic: AWS Bedrock LLM tool call arguments silently discarded, causing tools to receive empty input
signals.summary: When using AWS Bedrock LLM (e.g. Amazon Nova Pro), tool arguments are silently dropped. The LLM correctly calls the tool with arguments, but the tool receives an empty dict {}, causing TypeError or Pydantic ValidationError. Root cause: Bedrock Converse API format has no 'function' wrapper, so func_info.get('arguments', '{}') returns the default '{}' instead of falling through to tool_call.get('input', {}).
signals.review_reason: Confirmed bug with precise root cause. Breaks tool invocation for all AWS Bedrock users — every tool with required parameters fails silently with either TypeError or Pydantic ValidationError. Both affected versions (1.9.3, 1.13.0) are recent/stable. Count=1 because only this single issue exists, but user impact is high: blocks main workflow for Bedrock users and is easy to reproduce.

source_issues.title: [Bug] Bedrock tool call arguments silently dropped — tool invoked with empty input
source_issues.evidence: Confirmed in v1.9.3 and v1.13.0. LLM correctly calls tool with {"city": "Paris"} but tool receives {}. TypeError: missing required positional argument; or Pydantic ValidationError: Field required. Root cause traced to crewai/agents/crew_agent_executor.py _extract_tool_call_info.

signals.topic: BrightDataSearchTool uses JS template syntax (${query}) in Python f-strings, corrupting all search URLs
signals.summary: get_search_url in BrightDataSearchTool uses ${query} (JavaScript template literal syntax) instead of {query} in Python f-strings. This prepends a literal $ to every search query, producing broken URLs like https://www.google.com/search?q=$AI%20news instead of ?q=AI%20news. All three engines (Google, Bing, Yandex) are affected.
signals.review_reason: Confirmed bug with precise root cause and clear user impact. Every BrightDataSearchTool search query results in a broken URL with a $ prefix, causing the SERP API to return zero results or errors. Count=1 but all three search engines (Google, Bing, Yandex) are affected, making this a pervasive issue for any user relying on BrightData SERP.

source_issues.title: [BUG] BrightData SERP tool uses JavaScript template syntax in Python f-strings, breaking all search queries
source_issues.evidence: Confirmed bug. get_search_url() uses f-string with ${query} syntax. Python interprets ${query} as literal '$' + variable value, not as template interpolation. All three engines (google, bing, yandex) produce broken URLs. User's search queries are corrupted at the API level.

signals.topic: Regression in v1.11.1: PR #4656 fix for tool error handling and name collision resolution was accidentally reverted
signals.summary: Commit bb9bcd6 (March 30) removed _extract_tool_name() method as 'unused', but this method was part of PR #4656's fix for tool error handling and name collision resolution. v1.11.1 shipped with this regression. Impact: tools with duplicate names may not be distinguished correctly; tool execution errors may not be properly captured as observations; features relying on tool name mapping (result_as_answer, usage limits, caching) may malfunction.
aliases: PR 4656 regression broken tool error handling
signals.review_reason: Documented regression with clear timeline. PR #4656 fix was intentionally merged, verified working in v1.10.1, then accidentally broken in v1.11.1 by a cleanup commit that removed critical methods. This breaks core tool error handling for duplicate-named tools across multiple features. While count=1, the regression spans multiple user-facing features (error capture, name collision resolution, caching, result_as_answer) and affects a stable release.

source_issues.title: Regression: PR #4656 fix broken in v1.11.1 - Tool error handling and name collision resolution
source_issues.evidence: Timeline documented: PR #4656 (March 1) fixed tool error handling and name collision. v1.10.1 included fix and worked. Commit bb9bcd6 (March 30) removed _extract_tool_name() as cleanup. v1.11.1 shipped with the regression. Affected: tool name collision resolution, error observation capture, result_as_answer, usage limits, caching for duplicate-named tools.

signals.topic: Synchronous LLM call() blocks event loop in async workflows using output_json/output_pydantic
signals.summary: In async workflows started via akickoff(), when a Task has output_json or output_pydantic requiring format conversion, the converter module makes synchronous self.llm.call() which blocks the event loop. _export_output delegates to converter module, which is called from async Task methods. This causes async workflows to hang or crash when structured output is required.
aliases: akickoff event loop blocked by sync LLM
converter sync call in async context
signals.review_reason: Confirmed async/sync mismatch bug. Blocking the event loop with synchronous LLM calls in an async workflow is a well-defined anti-pattern that will cause hangs or crashes. Reproducible with akickoff() + structured output tasks. While the user couldn't provide a minimal reproduction snippet, the code path is traceable (task.py async methods -> _export_output -> converter -> sync llm.call()). Affects anyone using async crew workflows with structured output requirements.

source_issues.title: [BUG] Do not invoke synchronous call() on LLM from asynchronous workflow in _export_output / converter
source_issues.evidence: Async Task methods at task.py L605 and L1258 call _export_output, which delegates to converter module at task.py L1023. Converter module makes synchronous self.llm.call() calls in an async context, blocking the event loop. Reproducible by using akickoff() with Task(output_json=...) or Task(output_pydantic=...). OS: Debian 12, Python 3.12, crewAI 1.12.2.

signals.topic: InternalInstructor silently discards base_url for OpenAI-compatible providers, breaking vLLM/Ollama self-hosted endpoints
signals.summary: When using an OpenAI-compatible provider with a custom base_url (vLLM, Ollama, self-hosted endpoints), InternalInstructor's _create_instructor_client() extracts only model name and provider, then calls instructor.from_provider(). The base_url is never forwarded, causing all structured output requests (output_pydantic/output_json) to hit api.openai.com instead, resulting in ConnectTimeout for environments that cannot reach OpenAI.
signals.review_reason: Confirmed bug with complete code path analysis. Every user with a self-hosted OpenAI-compatible endpoint (vLLM, Ollama, custom endpoints) experiences ConnectTimeout errors on all structured output tasks (output_pydantic, output_json). The main LLM calls work fine — only the Converter/InternalInstructor path is broken. The root cause (base_url silently dropped) and affected code locations are precisely identified. Production impact is clear for self-hosted setups.

source_issues.title: [BUG] InternalInstructor discards base_url when creating instructor client — breaks OpenAI-compatible endpoints
source_issues.evidence: Full code path traced: converter.py L145-152 passes LLM object with base_url to InternalInstructor. internal_instructor.py L76-101 extracts only model and provider, calls instructor.from_provider() without base_url. _get_llm_extra_kwargs() exists but guarded by is_litellm=True, so non-LiteLLM OpenAI-compatible providers (vLLM, Ollama, Azure with custom endpoints) are all affected. Result: ConnectTimeout/ConverterError for all structured output tasks.

signals.topic: CLI fails to find Ollama vendor despite correct .env configuration, blocking remote inference requests
signals.summary: Fabric CLI and server cannot route requests through remote Ollama because the vendor registry fails to resolve DEFAULT_VENDOR=Ollama even when OLLAMA_API_URL/OLLAMA_BASE_URL are correctly set, returning 'could not find vendor' error and blocking the entire remote inference flow.
signals.review_reason: This is a main-flow blocking bug: the primary use case of routing CLI requests to a remote Ollama instance is entirely broken. The vendor registry lookup fails silently after the CLI itself identifies the correct vendor and URL, preventing any remote inference from completing. The user impact is clear: zero remote Ollama requests succeed even with correct configuration.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: "could not find vendor" error despite correctly configured .env (Ollama/Remote)
source_issues.evidence: CLI prints 'Default Vendor = Ollama' in logs but immediately fails with 'could not find vendor', blocking any remote Ollama request routing. User confirms `fabric -L` successfully lists remote models, proving network reachability, yet chat/stream logic fails to map model to vendor.

signals.topic: Fabric server hangs indefinitely at Context= stage when using remote Ollama provider, causing ECONNRESET
signals.summary: The `--serve` server hangs at the 'Context=' log stage indefinitely when connecting to a remote Ollama instance, eventually causing a socket hang up (ECONNRESET) in the Vite proxy. The server fails to stream tokens and the connection becomes a zombie until timeout, making remote Ollama usage via the server completely unusable.
signals.review_reason: This is a main-flow blocking bug for server-mode users: the `--serve` endpoint becomes completely unusable with remote Ollama, hanging until timeout. The issue blocks the entire server streaming workflow, which is a key deployment mode. User impact is unambiguous: connection zombie-ifies and produces no output.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: Server hangs at Context= when using remote Ollama provider (ECONNRESET)
source_issues.evidence: Server logs show 'Processing prompt 1: Model=glm-4.7-flash:latest Pattern=extract_insights Context=' and then hangs indefinitely. Connection eventually times out with ECONNRESET in the proxy. The remote Ollama instance is reachable (confirmed by `fabric -L` and curl), but the server-side streaming handshake fails silently.

signals.topic: Tool access permission repeatedly requested even in auto-accept / plan execution mode
signals.summary: Users with auto-accept edits mode or during plan execution are repeatedly blocked by 'no tool access permission' prompts, even after approving. The agent cannot proceed with its plan, blocking the main execution flow.
signals.review_reason: User explicitly reports plan execution is blocked because the agent keeps requesting tool permission approval even after user approves. The 'possible-duplicate' label suggests this is a known recurring pattern, not an isolated incident. This is a main-flow blocking issue: even in auto-accept mode, the agent cannot proceed.

source_issues.title: constantly complaining about no tool access permission even in auto-accept edits mode
source_issues.evidence: User reports agent repeatedly asks for tool approval even after user approves, blocking plan execution. Label 'status/possible-duplicate' suggests this is a known recurring pattern.

signals.topic: Paying Google One AI Premium subscriber blocked by 403 PERMISSION_DENIED due to server-side ghost project ID
signals.summary: Verified Google One AI Premium subscribers are blocked from using the service because the extension auto-injects an inaccessible 'ghost' Google Cloud project ID after OAuth login, causing all API calls to fail with 403. This is a cost-blocking issue for paying users.
signals.review_reason: This is a clear cost-blocking issue: a paying subscriber cannot use the service they paid for. The 403 PERMISSION_DENIED error completely prevents all API usage. The 'possible-duplicate' label and citation of community reports indicate this is a systemic issue affecting multiple subscribers, not an isolated incident.

source_issues.title: 403 PERMISSION_DENIED for Google One AI Premium subscriber - VS Code extension auto-injects inaccessible Ghost Project ID after OAuth login
source_issues.evidence: Verified paying subscriber cannot use the service at all. All API calls fail with 403. The issue cites community reports (#24517, #24425) indicating this affects multiple personal subscribers. The phantom project is server-side so local cleanup cannot resolve it.

signals.topic: Tool sandboxing blocks creation of tmp session directory, preventing plan/task writes and blocking default enablement
signals.summary: Tool sandboxing prevents the creation of temporary session directories, which breaks plan and task file writing. This is explicitly marked as a blocker for enabling tool sandboxing by default.
signals.review_reason: Explicitly identified by maintainers as a 'blocker' for enabling tool sandboxing by default. Additionally breaks plan/task writing for users who already have sandboxing enabled. This is a key security feature being blocked from default enablement.

source_issues.title: Fix creation of tmp session directory with tool sandboxing enabled
source_issues.evidence: Explicitly stated as a blocker: 'This is a blocker for enabling tool sandboxing by default.' Tool sandboxing is a core security feature, and this bug prevents its default activation while also breaking plan/task writing for users who manually enable it.

signals.topic: Agent enters infinite thinking/loop mode consuming excessive output and disrupting UX
signals.summary: When given certain prompts (e.g., a casual/social message like 'preciso dormir' / 'need sleep'), the agent enters an infinite thinking loop generating thousands of repeated words, flooding the terminal with nonsensical output and making the CLI unusable.
signals.review_reason: Agent enters a runaway loop that floods the terminal with thousands of repeated words, rendering the CLI completely unusable. This is a severe UX degradation where the main interaction loop breaks — the user cannot proceed with any task.

source_issues.title: infinite crazy thinking after prompt 'preciso dormir' (need sleep)
source_issues.evidence: Terminal output floods with thousands of repeated action verbs (scanning, processing, interpreting, etc.), creating an unusable state. The console goes 'full crazy' with continuous output, making the CLI completely unusable for the user.

signals.topic: Shell commands sometimes display no description, causing user confusion
signals.summary: When shell commands are executed, the description field is sometimes empty, leaving users confused about what command was run. Should at minimum show the command itself as the description.
signals.review_reason: Priority/P1 label assigned by maintainers. The shell tool description being empty creates UX confusion — users cannot see what command was executed. While not flow-blocking, it is a clear and acknowledged UX issue that degrades the transparency of agent actions.

source_issues.title: Shell commands sometimes lack a description
source_issues.evidence: Priority/P1 label assigned by triagers. Empty description visible in screenshot, user reports confusion when seeing no label for executed shell commands. This degrades the transparency of agent actions.

signals.topic: ManagedAgent silently swallows sub-agent failures, returning None/empty result to manager
signals.summary: When a sub-agent fails (tool error or max_steps exhaustion) inside a ManagedAgent wrapper, it returns None or empty string to the manager. The manager cannot distinguish failure from empty output, causing retry loops or hallucinated results.
aliases: sub-agent failure not propagated to manager
silent sub-agent failure in multi-agent pipeline
signals.review_reason: This is a real production multi-agent reliability issue. Silent sub-agent failures cause the manager to either loop or hallucinate results. The issue provides a full reproducible code example demonstrating the failure mode. Although count=1, the severity is high (full pipeline corruption possible) and the failure mode is subtle/difficult to debug in production.

source_issues.title: ManagedAgent swallows tool errors from sub-agents - manager sees empty/None result
source_issues.evidence: Sub-agent in multi-agent setup hits tool error or max_steps exhaustion; ManagedAgent returns empty/None result. Manager cannot distinguish 'task completed with empty output' from 'task failed'. Manager retries same sub-agent in a loop or proceeds with incorrect assumptions. Reproducer provided with CodeAgent + LiteLLMModel + ManagedAgent showing web_searcher fails silently.

signals.topic: No built-in retry/backoff for transient model API errors in MultiStepAgent
signals.summary: When a model API call inside MultiStepAgent.run() hits a transient error (429 rate limit, 503 unavailable, network timeout), the entire agent run fails immediately. Long multi-step tasks lose all progress on the last step with no recovery.
aliases: transient API errors cause full agent run failure
no retry on rate limit 429 in agent step loop
long multi-step task progress lost on single step failure
signals.review_reason: Clear user pain: transient API errors (rate limits, timeouts) immediately abort entire long-running agent tasks with no retry, causing full progress loss. Users must write boilerplate retry wrappers per project. Reproducer with LiteLLMModel and 10-step task provided. This is a direct cost-of-retry and workflow-abort issue.

source_issues.title: No built-in retry/backoff for transient model API errors in MultiStepAgent
source_issues.evidence: Entire agent run fails immediately on rate limit 429 or 503. For a 10-step task, failure at step 8 loses all prior progress. No built-in retry mechanism. Users must subclass the model with custom retry logic, which is non-obvious and duplicated. Workaround requires wrapping LiteLLMModel.__call__ with retry logic per-project.

signals.topic: VisitWebpageTool returns unbounded content, silently overflowing model context window
signals.summary: VisitWebpageTool fetches full page text with no size cap. Large pages (Wikipedia, SEC filings, docs) return 80KB+ of text causing silent context window overflow. Error manifests as LLM API error, masking the root cause.
aliases: webpage tool context overflow without error signal
signals.review_reason: User pain is real: large web pages silently cause context overflow, making the failure appear as an LLM bug rather than a tool configuration issue. This wastes API credits and causes confusing debugging sessions. Although count=1 and issue is closed, the failure mode is common for any user who asks agents to summarize Wikipedia or long articles.

source_issues.title: VisitWebpageTool has no response size limit and can silently overflow context window
source_issues.evidence: Tool returns 80KB+ of text from large pages. Model silently gets truncated result or fails at API call level with context length error that appears to be an LLM bug rather than a tool bug. No user-facing error from the tool itself. DuckDuckGoSearchTool already has max_results; VisitWebpageTool lacks equivalent size limit.

signals.topic: WebSearchTool hardcoded 30-second HTTP timeout causes agent run abort in slow/corporate networks
signals.summary: All WebSearchTool backends use hardcoded timeout=30. In corporate proxy or slow-network environments, legitimate requests exceed 30s causing ReadTimeout that aborts the agent run. Users cannot override without subclassing.
aliases: hardcoded HTTP timeout breaks corporate networks
signals.review_reason: Hardcoded network timeout causes agent runs to abort on ReadTimeout in legitimate slow-network or corporate proxy scenarios. Users cannot configure without subclassing. The issue also notes the Exa backend introduced in PR #2139 has zero timeout at all, creating inconsistent behavior. Although count=1, the user impact is a hard block on agent execution in any constrained network environment.

source_issues.title: Make HTTP request timeout configurable in WebSearchTool
source_issues.evidence: All three search backends (google, bing, duckduckgo) use hardcoded timeout=30. Exa backend added in PR #2139 has no timeout at all. Corporate proxies and slow networks cause legitimate requests to exceed 30s. No user-facing config to override. Agent run is aborted on ReadTimeout with no retry.

signals.topic: Missing Groq integration documentation drives users to use incompatible ToolCallingAgent
signals.summary: No documentation exists for using Groq with smolagents. Users find only open issues reporting failures with Groq, and attempt ToolCallingAgent which has known tool-call format incompatibilities with Groq. Users file duplicate issues unaware of the supported path.
aliases: no Groq docs, users try ToolCallingAgent and hit known bug
Groq integration path undocumented causing repeated bug reports
signals.review_reason: Documentation gap creates a recurring user experience failure: users hit the ToolCallingAgent+Groq incompatibility bug, file issues, and waste time. The issue explicitly links to three prior unresolved issues (#1119, #655, #429) all caused by the same documentation gap. Although the root bug is in Groq compatibility, the pain point is the missing documentation causing repeated user frustration.

source_issues.title: Add documentation and example for using CodeAgent with Groq via LiteLLMModel
source_issues.evidence: Users searching for Groq in the codebase find only open issues reporting failures (#1119, #655, #429). No guidance on the supported path (LiteLLMModel with groq/ prefix + CodeAgent). Every new user attempts ToolCallingAgent first, hits the tool-calling bug, and files a new issue. This is a known recurring pattern causing repeated support burden.

signals.topic: Codex API incompatible with autonomous research loop — model ignores 'never stop' instruction, breaking interactive sessions
signals.summary: Codex (OpenAI's coding model) does not respect the 'never stop' instruction required for autonomous research sessions, unlike Claude which handles it correctly. This causes Codex to stop prematurely, making it unusable for the core autonomous agent use case.
signals.review_reason: Issue #57 documents a real user pain point: the core autonomous research loop is fundamentally broken when using Codex as the backend model. The 'never stop' instruction is ignored, causing the model to stop mid-session — a direct block on the primary use case. 36 comments confirm sustained user impact and community interest. Unlike a generic model API difference, this specifically prevents the interactive autonomous workflow that is the stated purpose of the repo.

source_issues.title: Codex doesn't seem to work?
source_issues.evidence: 36 comments, actively discussed open issue. karpathy (repo owner) filed it. Codex ignores instruction to 'never stop', unlike Claude which works with /loop. Author prefers interactive session to observe agent work and contribute, but Codex stops prematurely, making the core autonomous workflow impossible.

signals.topic: Seed change counted as model improvement — confounds experiment trajectory and metric validity
signals.summary: Random seed changes are being logged as improvements in results.tsv, which can falsely inflate progress metrics. The agent may waste experiments repeating seed-based 'wins' that are statistical noise rather than genuine algorithmic gains.
aliases: Random seed wins tracked as progress
Lucky gains indistinguishable from real gains
signals.review_reason: Issue #466 describes a real concern about experiment metric validity: seed changes (random variation) are being logged as improvements, which can mislead the agent's experiment selection during autonomous runs. While not a hard crash or block, it degrades experiment quality and wastes compute on non-reproducible gains. This is a measurable cost loss (wasted experiments) and a non-trivial quality-of-research problem.

source_issues.title: change of seed registered as improvement?
source_issues.evidence: User raised concern that seed change shown in README graph is registered as a valid improvement step, but seed changes are effectively random luck. This risks the agent making suboptimal experiment selection decisions by treating noise as signal.

signals.topic: CLI and SDK expose different default agent behavior causing user confusion
signals.summary: The Deep Agents CLI and the create_deep_agent() SDK use different default system prompts. CLI uses a long coding-terminal brief while SDK uses a minimal base prompt, and the memory middleware injects conflicting prioritization rules. In headless/non-interactive mode, the prompt additionally contradicts itself by saying both 'do not ask questions' and 'wait for user response'. Users cannot rely on consistent agent behavior between CLI and programmatic usage.
signals.review_reason: Three separate issues all confirm the same root cause: divergent prompt specifications between CLI and SDK, and within the CLI itself in different modes. This causes the agent to exhibit inconsistent behavior, follow contradictory instructions, and leaves users debugging 'why does it work in CLI but not in my code?' confusion. It is a documented, reproducible behavioral difference that affects the core contract of the product.

source_issues.title: cli/sdk: default agent 'personality' differs between CLI and create_deep_agent()
source_issues.evidence: CLI default uses get_system_prompt() loading system_prompt.md (coding-terminal brief with 4-line answer rule, stop-without-explaining, git safety rules) concatenated with BASE_AGENT_PROMPT. SDK default create_deep_agent(system_prompt=None) uses only BASE_AGENT_PROMPT. Same API name, different defaults. Users report 'works in CLI, different in my app'. Duplicate/overlapping rules between the two prompt sources compete.

source_issues.title: Memory system prompt over-prioritizes edit_file over reads and other tools
source_issues.evidence: MEMORY_SYSTEM_PROMPT instructs agent to treat memory updates as MAIN PRIORITY and to call edit_file as FIRST IMMEDIATE action before responding to the user and before calling other tools. This directly conflicts with BASE_AGENT_PROMPT's 'understand first' workflow (read files, gather evidence, then act). Also, loaded memory content is not flagged as untrusted data, creating a prompt-injection risk.

source_issues.title: Conflicting instructions for todos in non-interactive mode in CLI
source_issues.evidence: In headless mode (interactive=False), get_system_prompt injects ambiguity guidance saying 'do NOT ask clarifying questions, make reasonable assumptions and proceed'. The same prompt still includes Todo List Management section requiring agent to 'ALWAYS ask the user if the plan looks good' and 'wait for the user's response before marking the first todo in_progress'. Self-contradictory instructions in a single prompt cause blocking or inconsistent agent behavior in automation.

signals.topic: Playwright browser tool call cancellation causes browser automation tasks to fail
signals.summary: Tool calls to playwright_browser_navigate are cancelled before completion with error 'Tool call was cancelled - another message came in before it could be completed', blocking web scraping, UI testing, and browser navigation workflows. Multiple users report this consistently.
signals.review_reason: Multiple users independently report the same playwright_browser_navigate cancellation error with identical message. This blocks the core browser automation use case of Deep Agents — web scraping, UI testing, and any workflow requiring browser navigation all fail. The error is reproducible and the impact is explicitly enumerated in issue bodies.

source_issues.title: Playwright Browser Tool Call Cancellation Error
source_issues.evidence: Tool call playwright_browser_navigate with id call_00_UCrWduKjhXp1jZiwBA6e52TT was cancelled - another message came in before it could be completed. Error reproduced with minimal example: playwright_browser_navigate(url='https://www.google.com') fails in Deep Agents CLI. Prevents web scraping, UI testing, and browser navigation.

source_issues.title: Playwright Browser Tool Call Cancellation Error
source_issues.evidence: Same error message: 'Tool call playwright_browser_navigate with id call_00_UCrWduKjhXp1jZiwBA6e52TT was cancelled'. Same root cause: concurrent message arrives before tool completes. Multiple impacts listed: browser automation tasks, web scraping operations, UI testing workflows.

signals.topic: Dependency conflict blocks deepagents-cli installation via pip
signals.summary: Installing deepagents-cli via pip pulls in langsmith[sandbox] which pins websockets<16, causing pip install to fail in any environment that requires websockets>=16. The user does not need LangSmith to encounter this failure.
signals.review_reason: A hard install failure for the CLI tool, the primary entry point for users. The conflict is systemic: any user on a project requiring websockets>=16 cannot install deepagents-cli at all, regardless of their intent to use LangSmith. This is a main-flow-blocking packaging defect.

source_issues.title: Make LangSmith sandbox optional in deepagents-cli to avoid websockets conflicts
source_issues.evidence: pip install deepagents-cli pulls in langsmith[sandbox] which pins websockets<16. In environments requiring websockets>=16, pip install fails immediately. This occurs even when the user has no intention of using LangSmith or Daytona sandboxes — the dependency is forced on all installs.

signals.topic: Filesystem tools crash the agent with hard exception on invalid file paths
signals.summary: edit_file and other filesystem tools crash with an unhandled exception when given an invalid file path (e.g. a path containing special characters). The agent hard-lands and cannot recover or retry, breaking the task flow entirely.
signals.review_reason: A hard crash in a core filesystem tool that terminates the agent instead of providing a recoverable error. The agent cannot retry or self-correct, which blocks any task flow relying on file editing. While lower frequency, this is a main-flow failure with explicit user impact and a clear fix direction.

source_issues.title: Filesystem tools crashes on invalid file path
source_issues.evidence: edit_file raises unhandled exception: 'Error: File /email_request_05-04-2021? not found' with full Python traceback exposed to the agent. The agent crashes with a hard landing instead of receiving a graceful error it can act on. The issue author explicitly requests: 'Suggest the filesystem tool to respond to the agent so that they could work together to retry instead of this hard-landing crashes.' Occurs in production with paths containing question marks and likely other special characters.

signals.topic: read_file pagination skips lines when files contain long wrapped lines
signals.summary: When a file contains very long lines that wrap across multiple display rows, read_file pagination applies limits twice (once for backend fetch, once for display offset), causing wrapped lines and subsequent lines to be skipped entirely. The pagination offset advances past lines that were never shown.
signals.review_reason: A logic bug in read_file pagination that silently skips important file content. When long lines are present, subsequent lines are permanently excluded from the agent's view. This is a main-flow issue affecting any codebase with long lines (common in generated/minified code, logs, or config files), with an explicit reproduction and clear root cause identified.

source_issues.title: read_file pagination skips lines after wrapping due to double limit application
source_issues.evidence: When a long line is wrapped into multiple display rows, only part of the formatted output is returned even though the backend already fetched the next line. Pagination then continues from a later offset, so the wrapped line and content immediately following it are never shown. Reproduction provided with a 15000-character line followed by 'important instruction' — the important instruction is skipped on second page. This is a silent data loss issue.

signals.topic: langchain-ollama crashes with `cannot unmarshal array into Go value` when tool calls contain array arguments
signals.summary: Agent workflow crashes completely when langchain-ollama receives a tool call with array arguments, due to JSON type mismatch in the Ollama API response parsing.
aliases: Ollama tool call array argument parsing failure
signals.review_reason: This causes complete agent crash — a full main flow failure that blocks any workflow using tools with array arguments. The crash is a JSON type mismatch in the Ollama API response, producing a non-recoverable exception that terminates the entire agent run. Count=1 but P0 due to total workflow blocking with clear stack trace evidence.

source_issues.title: `cannot unmarshal array into Go value of type api.ToolCallFunctionArguments (status code: -1)`
source_issues.evidence: Agent crashes with error: 'ollama._types.ResponseError: error parsing tool call: raw=[{...}], err=json: cannot unmarshal array into Go value of type api.ToolCallFunctionArguments (status code: -1)'. Full stack trace shows crash in langchain_ollama/chat_models.py at _agenerate -> _achat_stream_with_aggregation -> _aiterate_over_stream -> _acreate_chat_stream. Any agent workflow using tools with array arguments is completely blocked.

signals.topic: ChatBedrockConverse permanently breaks after ModelFallbackMiddleware fires Azure OpenAI Responses API fallback
signals.summary: Once ModelFallbackMiddleware triggers a fallback to Azure OpenAI Responses API, ChatBedrockConverse permanently crashes on that thread due to unsupported function_call content block serialization in checkpoint history.
aliases: Bedrock function_call serialization crash after fallback
signals.review_reason: This causes a permanent main flow failure for the Bedrock thread. After the fallback fires once, Bedrock becomes permanently unusable on that thread due to unsupported function_call checkpoint serialization. This is a critical production bug for systems using ModelFallbackMiddleware — the failure is irreversible and affects every subsequent turn in the conversation.

source_issues.title: ChatBedrockConverse crashes on function_call content blocks from OpenAI Responses API when used with ModelFallbackMiddleware
source_issues.evidence: _lc_content_to_bedrock() raises ValueError: Unsupported content block type when message history contains function_call content blocks produced by OpenAI Responses API (use_responses_api=True). When ModelFallbackMiddleware fires the fallback (AzureChatOpenAI with Responses API), the resulting function_call blocks are checkpointed. On subsequent turns, Bedrock tries to serialize this history and crashes permanently. Once the fallback fires, Bedrock is permanently broken for that thread.

signals.topic: ChatOllama `bind_tools()` with complex schema silently drops all reasoning output when system prompt is large
signals.summary: When using ChatOllama with reasoning models (gemma4:26b) and bind_tools() on a complex tool schema combined with a large system prompt, reasoning tokens are completely and silently suppressed.
signals.review_reason: This causes a key feature (reasoning transparency) to be silently suppressed in production agent workflows. The model still produces text output so the flow is not fully blocked, but reasoning_content is a critical debugging and transparency feature for agent workflows. The suppression is silent with no error thrown, making it hard for users to diagnose.

source_issues.title: `ChatOllama.bind_tools()` with large system prompt suppresses reasoning output on gemma4:26b
source_issues.evidence: When ChatOllama is configured with reasoning=True and used with bind_tools() on a tool with moderately complex schema combined with a large system prompt (~2-3k tokens), gemma4:26b stops emitting reasoning_content entirely. Output shows: 'tools, big prompt: {reasoning: 0, text: 7}' — reasoning silently dropped. Bisection confirmed: large prompt alone = reasoning present, simple tool alone = reasoning present, complex tool + small prompt = reasoning present, complex tool + large prompt = reasoning drops to zero. The drop is silent with no error.

signals.topic: `wrap_model_call` middleware ToolStrategy narrowing is validated but never enforced — model sees all tools regardless
signals.summary: When middleware attempts to narrow the response_format from a union ToolStrategy to a single-type subset via @wrap_model_call, the narrowing is validated but completely ignored, and the model still sees all structured output tools.
aliases: ToolStrategy subset narrowing has no effect
signals.review_reason: This breaks the documented contract of middleware narrowing in agent building. Users who rely on state-dependent structured output (a core agent design pattern) find their tool restrictions silently ignored. The model can produce any output format from the original union regardless of middleware intent, making agent state transitions unreliable.

source_issues.title: `wrap_model_call` middleware ToolStrategy narrowing has no effect — model still sees all structured output tools
source_issues.evidence: When @wrap_model_call middleware narrows response_format from a union ToolStrategy to a single-type subset via request.override(response_format=ToolStrategy(SubsetType)), the narrowing is validated (lines 1241-1248 of factory.py confirm the subset is valid) but never enforced. All structured output tools from the original union are always bound to the model. The model can choose any of them regardless of middleware narrowing, contradicting documented behavior and breaking state-dependent structured output workflows.

signals.topic: _convert_messages_to_ollama_messages mutates caller's message list in-place as hidden side effect
signals.summary: The internal method _convert_messages_to_ollama_messages in chat_models.py silently modifies the caller's message list as a side effect, which can cause hard-to-debug state corruption in complex workflows.
signals.review_reason: This is a hidden state corruption bug that violates the principle of least surprise. The method mutates a parameter it does not own as a side effect, which can cause non-deterministic behavior in any code path that holds references to the message list. The incidental protection in invoke/generate is undocumented and fragile — any refactor or new caller would expose the corruption.

source_issues.title: fix(ollama): _convert_messages_to_ollama_messages mutates caller's list in-place
source_issues.evidence: _convert_messages_to_ollama_messages() in chat_models.py modifies the list it receives as a parameter. When it encounters an AIMessage whose response_metadata['output_version'] == 'v1', it silently replaces that element in the caller's list. The bug is currently hidden because BaseChatModel.invoke() and BaseChatModel.generate() happen to pass a shallow copy of the list to _generate(). This protection is entirely incidental and undocumented, meaning any direct caller or future code change would trigger unexpected state corruption.

signals.topic: Background runs silently re-executed on LangGraph Cloud causing 2-3x cost multiplication
signals.summary: Tool calls taking >180s are silently re-dispatched from checkpoint while original is still running, completing twice and causing redundant cost. Additionally, executor 0.7.96 crashes all LangGraph Cloud first runs with RuntimeError about execution_info.
signals.review_reason: Two LangGraph Cloud issues: #7417 causes silent cost multiplication (2-3x extra work) due to heartbeat-based re-dispatch. #7420 causes complete blocking crash on all first runs. Both affect production deployments with no user workaround.

source_issues.title: Long tool calls (~180s+) silently re-executed from checkpoint
source_issues.evidence: Tool calls taking >180s are silently re-dispatched from checkpoint while original is still running. Both complete successfully, causing 2-3x redundant work and cost. Users cannot detect this without inspecting traces.

source_issues.title: RuntimeError: Cannot patch execution_info before it has been set
source_issues.evidence: Every graph deployed to LangGraph Cloud crashes on first run with RuntimeError. Verified working on executor 0.7.94, broken on 0.7.96.

signals.topic: Checkpoint/resume replays from beginning instead of continuing from interrupt
signals.summary: Resume from interrupt with specific checkpoint_id runs from graph beginning instead of interrupt trigger point. Cancellation also loses all streamed state not yet persisted.
signals.review_reason: Two issues affecting checkpoint integrity: #7361 causes resume to replay from beginning instead of continuing from interrupt, breaking conversational continuity. #5672 causes streamed state to be lost on cancellation. Both represent main flow failures where user's perceived progress is lost.

source_issues.title: When resume from a specific checkpoint_id, it becomes replay
source_issues.evidence: Resume from interrupt with specific checkpoint_id runs from graph beginning instead of interrupt trigger point. Expected output shows messages from interrupt onwards, but actual output only shows final message, breaking user workflow continuity.

source_issues.title: Run Cancellation Causes Loss of Streamed State Not Yet Persisted
source_issues.evidence: Canceling a LangGraph run during streaming loses all streamed state not yet persisted as checkpoint. Users see output for seconds but after cancel it disappears.

signals.topic: Parallel tool call errors discard all successful sibling results
signals.summary: When ToolNode executes parallel tools via asyncio.gather and one raises non-ToolInvocationError, successful results from sibling tools are discarded.
signals.review_reason: UX degradation when one parallel tool fails: all successful tool results are discarded. Users expect partial success (completed tools should keep their results). Affects any multi-tool parallel workflow with no intuitive workaround.

source_issues.title: Default handle_tool_errors doesn't catch tool execution errors in parallel calls
source_issues.evidence: When ToolNode executes multiple parallel tool calls via asyncio.gather and one raises non-ToolInvocationError (e.g. ValueError, HTTPError), the exception propagates and discards successful results from sibling tools. User expects partial success but gets full failure.

signals.topic: InMemoryStore overwrites created_at on update causing backend inconsistency
signals.summary: InMemoryStore._apply_put_ops unconditionally overwrites created_at on every put, unlike PostgresStore which preserves it, causing behavioral differences across backends.
signals.review_reason: Data inconsistency: InMemoryStore loses created_at on every update while PostgresStore preserves it. Users testing with InMemoryStore and deploying with PostgresStore get different staleness query or ordering results.

source_issues.title: InMemoryStore.put() overwrites created_at on update
source_issues.evidence: InMemoryStore._apply_put_ops unconditionally sets created_at=datetime.now() on every put, even for updates. PostgresStore correctly preserves created_at via ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE. Code relying on created_at for ordering/staleness gets different results per backend.

signals.topic: langgraph-prebuilt v1.0.9 incompatible with langgraph < 1.1.0 causing ImportError
signals.summary: ImportError: cannot import name 'ServerInfo' prevents any user with pinned langgraph < 1.1.0 from importing langgraph.prebuilt.
signals.review_reason: Complete blocking failure: any user with pinned langgraph < 1.1.0 cannot import langgraph.prebuilt at all. No workaround except unpinning/updating. Affects users who locked dependencies for stability.

source_issues.title: langgraph-prebuilt v1.0.9 breaks with older versions of langgraph
source_issues.evidence: ImportError: cannot import name 'ServerInfo' from 'langgraph.runtime'. Users with langgraph==1.1.3 pinned cannot use langgraph-prebuilt. Breaking change released as minor version bump.

signals.topic: Database migration failure after version upgrade causes 500 Internal Server Error blocking all dataset access
signals.summary: Self-hosted Docker users encounter 500 errors on all dataset API calls after upgrading Dify due to missing database column 'datasets.summary_index_setting'. The migration fails to apply schema changes, making the platform completely unusable.
signals.review_reason: Critical main flow failure. After upgrading (even across minor versions), users get 500 errors on all dataset API calls due to missing database column. Users cannot access datasets at all — complete block of primary platform functionality for self-hosted users who upgrade.

source_issues.title: [BUG] 500 Internal Server Error after upgrading from old version to new commit
source_issues.evidence: User upgrading from 1.11.4 to 1.13.3 encounters 500 error on all dataset API calls. Error: 'column datasets.summary_index_setting does not exist'. User rolled back to 1.12.0 but error persisted. Platform completely unusable for self-hosted Docker users after upgrade.

signals.topic: Knowledge Retrieval node returns empty results [] after v1.13.x update despite correct chunks in retrieval testing panel
signals.summary: Knowledge Retrieval workflow node silently returns empty results [] after v1.13.x update even though the same query returns correct chunks in the Retrieval Testing panel, breaking RAG workflows.
signals.review_reason: Core RAG functionality failure. Knowledge Retrieval is a primary workflow node for building LLM applications with context. Users report empty results despite the retrieval testing panel showing correct chunks for the same query — workflows silently fail. Regression in v1.13.x affecting the knowledge retrieval node execution path.

source_issues.title: Knowledge Retrieval node returns [] most of the time after v1.13.x update (HQ-HYBRID + reranker + metadata filter)
source_issues.evidence: KR node returns empty [] with STATUS: SUCCESS and 0 Tokens. Same query in Retrieval Testing panel correctly returns chunks with scores 0.85-0.99. Issue only affects v1.13.x. Workflows relying on knowledge retrieval fail silently.

signals.topic: Parameter Extractor node fails with unmarshal error on v1.13.3
signals.summary: Parameter Extractor workflow node fails completely on v1.13.3 with 'unmarshal json failed: content field is required', blocking workflows that depend on structured parameter extraction.
signals.review_reason: Main flow failure for workflows using Parameter Extractor. Node fails completely on v1.13.3 with clear error. Parameter Extractor is commonly used to extract structured parameters from LLM responses for downstream workflow steps. Users on v1.13.3 cannot use this node at all, blocking workflows that depend on structured parameter extraction.

source_issues.title: [Bug] Parameter Extractor node fails with 'unmarshal json failed: content field is required' on v1.13.3
source_issues.evidence: Parameter Extractor node fails with error 'unmarshal json failed: content field is required'. Tested with gpt-5.2, gpt-5-mini, gpt-4o-mini — all fail. Root cause: GPT-5 series models routed to Responses API, content conversion logic does not handle all content types correctly.

signals.topic: In-flight workflow executions not resumed after api-worker service crash leaving workflows stranded
signals.summary: When api-worker service crashes or restarts during workflow execution in v1.13.3, in-flight workflows stay in 'Running' state forever and are permanently lost with no recovery mechanism.
signals.review_reason: Significant reliability/cost issue for production deployments. When api-worker crashes during workflow execution, in-flight workflows are permanently lost — they stay in 'Running' state forever. User work is lost with no recovery. For production deployments running long workflows, unexpected restarts can lose significant work.

source_issues.title: Make workflow executions resumable after api-worker service crash
source_issues.evidence: In v1.13.3, streaming workflow execution is dispatched to workflow_based_app_execution_task on the worker side. When api-worker crashes during execution, in-flight workflows are not resumed. Screenshot shows workflow forever 'Running' after crash. User states 'a service crash can leave a workflow run stranded forever or effectively lost instead of resumed.'

signals.topic: Azure OpenAI TTS hardcodes mp3 response_format causing file extension mismatch with actual audio content
signals.summary: Azure TTS node hardcodes response_format='mp3' in code but outputs files with .wav extension, producing corrupted/unusable audio files. Users cannot select different audio formats even though the API supports them.
signals.review_reason: Clear cost loss and user frustration. Users configure Azure TTS expecting wav output based on model settings, but receive mp3 content in a .wav file. Audio file is effectively corrupted and unusable. Hardcoded format means users cannot select different audio formats even when the API supports them, wasting API calls and user time.

source_issues.title: Azure OpenAI TTS: response_format is hardcoded to 'mp3', ignoring model_properties.audio_type
source_issues.evidence: Azure TTS node hardcodes response_format='mp3' in code but outputs file with .wav extension. User downloads audio expecting wav but gets mp3 content. OpenAI API supports mp3, opus, aac, flac, wav, pcm formats but user cannot select. File is corrupted/unusable.

signals.topic: openclaw-mem0 crashes/fails when using pgvector in OSS mode — client reuse error and memory operation failures
signals.summary: When @mem0/openclaw-mem0 is configured with pgvector in OSS mode, memory initialization fails, recall times out, and subsequent operations fail with repeated 'Client has already been connected. You cannot reuse a client.' errors. This is a critical integration bug that blocks the primary memory workflow in OpenClaw.
signals.review_reason: Two confirmed bug reports from the same repo (4727 + 4638) both showing the same pgvector client-reuse error that completely blocks memory initialization and recall in OSS mode. This is a primary use-case failure — users cannot use openclaw-mem0 with pgvector at all. High confidence, directly witnessed user impact.

source_issues.title: [Bug][OpenClaw][OSS/pgvector] openclaw-mem0 crashes/fails when using pgvector in OSS mode
source_issues.evidence: Memory initialization fails, recall times out, subsequent operations fail with 'Client has already been connected. You cannot reuse a client.' error. Plugin registration succeeds but all memory operations are blocked.

source_issues.title: openclaw plugin error with pgvector
source_issues.evidence: openclaw mem0 stats shows error 'Client has already been connected. You cannot reuse a client.' during PGVector.initialize in mem0ai/dist/oss/index.mjs. Confirmed pgvector connection reuse bug.

signals.topic: OpenAILLM JS SDK ignores timeout config — add() hangs indefinitely on slow/unresponsive LLM responses
signals.summary: The OpenAILLM constructor in the JS OSS SDK does not forward the timeout configuration to the OpenAI client. The OpenAI JS SDK's default timeout is 10 minutes, meaning any unresponsive LLM backend will block the event loop for up to 10 minutes. Additionally, when the LLM returns an out-of-range action.id, updateMemory/deleteMemory are called with undefined IDs.
aliases: event loop blocked 10 minutes slow response
signals.review_reason: Two confirmed bug reports (4707 + 4708) describing the same root cause: timeout not forwarded to the OpenAI JS client. The result is a 10-minute blocking hang on the Node.js event loop for any slow LLM backend — a severe degradation of the primary memory.add() workflow. This is a well-documented, reproducible bug with a clear root cause in the OSS TypeScript SDK.

source_issues.title: [Bug][JS OSS] updateMemory/deleteMemory called with undefined ID when LLM returns out-of-range action.id
source_issues.evidence: Memory.add() hangs indefinitely when LLM backend is slow or non-responsive. Root cause: OpenAILLM constructor in src/oss/src/llms/openai.ts does NOT pass timeout to OpenAI client. Default timeout is 10 minutes, blocking event loop for up to 10 min. When LLM returns out-of-range action.id, updateMemory/deleteMemory are called with undefined IDs.

source_issues.title: [Bug][JS OSS] OpenAILLM ignores timeout config — add() hangs indefinitely on slow LLM responses
source_issues.evidence: OpenAILLM constructor does not forward timeout to the OpenAI client, causing add() to hang indefinitely on slow LLM responses. Includes detailed reproduction code with slow mock server showing expected vs actual behavior. Event loop blocked for full duration.

signals.topic: Groq LLM integration broken — deprecated default model and duplicate base URL path causing 404 errors
signals.summary: Two Groq integration bugs: (1) the default Groq model llama3-70b-8192 is deprecated and returns 400 errors, (2) Mem0 incorrectly appends /openai/v1 to Groq's base URL which already contains it, resulting in 404 errors. Users cannot use Groq as an LLM provider in either case.
signals.review_reason: Two confirmed bugs affecting the same integration target (Groq LLM). Both are distinct issues that independently break Groq integration: (1) deprecated model causing 400 errors, (2) base URL duplication causing 404 errors. Groq is a popular free/subsidized LLM provider for developers; these bugs completely block its use as an mem0 backend.

source_issues.title: Default Groq model is deprecated (llama3-70b-8192)
source_issues.evidence: Default Groq model llama3-70b-8192 is deprecated and causes a 400 error when using Groq as LLM provider. Error message confirms model has been decommissioned. Reproduction code provided.

source_issues.title: Groq base_url handling causes duplicate /openai/v1 path in Mem0 leading to 404 error
source_issues.evidence: When using Groq as LLM via OpenAI-compatible API (https://api.groq.com/openai/v1), Mem0 appends /openai/v1 again, resulting in invalid endpoint https://api.groq.com/openai/v1/openai/v1/chat/completions and a 404 error. Confirmed by reproduction.

signals.topic: autoRecall/autoCapture hooks block Node.js event loop — LLM calls serialize all concurrent operations
signals.summary: In OSS mode, the autoRecall and autoCapture hooks perform synchronous blocking LLM calls on the Node.js main event loop, causing the event loop to stall for the full duration of LLM calls (1-40s) and serializing all concurrent async operations. This is a critical performance and concurrency bug in OpenClaw integration.
aliases: event loop stall on LLM hooks
signals.review_reason: OpenClaw integration with Mem0 OSS is a documented use case. The autoRecall/autoCapture hooks performing synchronous blocking LLM calls is a severe concurrency bug that directly impacts the primary event loop of any Node.js application using mem0 as a plugin — blocking all concurrent operations for up to 40 seconds per call. This is not an edge case but a systemic architectural flaw in the OSS Node.js integration path.

source_issues.title: autoRecall/autoCapture hooks make synchronous blocking LLM calls on Node.js event loop
source_issues.evidence: autoRecall and autoCapture hooks in OSS mode make synchronous blocking LLM calls on the Node.js main event loop when used as OpenClaw plugin. Event loop stalls for full duration of LLM call (typically 1-40s), serializing all concurrent async operations. This breaks core concurrency assumptions in Node.js environments.

signals.topic: Ollama/custom embedding models with non-1536 dimensions cause silent dimension mismatch with Qdrant
signals.summary: When using Ollama as embedding provider with models that output non-default dimensions (e.g. bge-m3: 1024, nomic-embed-text: 768), the Qdrant vector store collection is created with the hardcoded default of 1536 dimensions. This causes dimension mismatch errors or silent failures on memory operations.
signals.review_reason: This is a concrete integration bug between a popular embedding provider (Ollama) and a popular vector store (Qdrant). The dimension mismatch causes operations to fail silently or with obscure errors. The most common Ollama embedding models (bge-m3, nomic-embed-text) are affected, making this a high-reach issue for self-hosted deployments.

source_issues.title: Ollama embedding dimensions not propagated to Qdrant vector store (bge-m3: 1024 vs hardcoded 1536)
source_issues.evidence: Qdrant collection is created with hardcoded 1536 dimensions even when Ollama model outputs different dimensions (bge-m3: 1024, nomic-embed-text: 768). Results in dimension mismatch errors or silent failures on memory operations. No user-facing error until retrieval fails completely.

signals.topic: agent-framework 1.0.0 incompatible with azure-ai-agentserver-agentframework 1.0.0b17 — pip install fails
signals.summary: agent-framework 1.0.0 与 azure-ai-agentserver-agentframework 1.0.0b17 存在依赖冲突，导致 pip install 失败，阻断用户将框架 Agent 部署为 Azure Foundry Hosted Agent 的核心流程
signals.review_reason: pip install 直接失败，完全阻断用户将 agent-framework Agent 部署为 Azure Foundry Hosted Agent 的核心工作流程。有明确的依赖冲突证据（agent-framework 1.0.0 需要 agent-framework-core==1.0.0，而 azure-ai-agentserver-agentframework 1.0.0b17 需要 <=1.0.0rc3），非边缘问题。

source_issues.title: Python: [Bug]: 1.0.0 Incompatible with azure-ai-agentserver-agentframework==1.0.0b17
source_issues.evidence: pip install fails with dependency conflict: azure-ai-agentserver-agentframework 1.0.0b17 depends on agent-framework-core<=1.0.0rc3 while agent-framework 1.0.0 requires agent-framework-core==1.0.0. User cannot deploy their agent as a Foundry Hosted Agent, blocking their core deployment workflow.

signals.topic: agent-framework-github-copilot import breaks with github-copilot-sdk >= 0.2.0 — ModuleNotFoundError
signals.summary: github-copilot-sdk 升级到 0.2.x 后，agent-framework-github-copilot 在 import 时即抛出 ModuleNotFoundError，阻断该扩展包所有使用场景
aliases: copilot.types module not found after SDK upgrade
signals.review_reason: import 时即崩溃（ModuleNotFoundError），完全阻断 GitHub Copilot 集成所有使用场景。有完整堆栈和受影响文件列表，SDK 升级导致类型路径重新组织，属于主流程阻断。

source_issues.title: Python: [Bug]: GitHub Copilot package incompatible with github-copilot-sdk 0.2.x
source_issues.evidence: Importing agent_framework_github_copilot raises ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'copilot.types'. SDK 0.2.x reorganized types across multiple modules (copilot.generated.session_events, copilot.session, copilot.client, copilot.tools). Affected files: _agent.py, tests, and all 7 samples. Any user upgrading github-copilot-sdk to 0.2.x has their Copilot agent completely broken.

signals.topic: Content.from_uri base64 image regression in FoundryChatClient — HTTP 400 on valid base64 image data
signals.summary: agent-framework 1.0.0 中使用 Content.from_uri 发送 base64 图片数据时返回 HTTP 400 错误，提示数据不符合预期 schema，导致图片上传功能完全不可用
aliases: base64 image data rejected with 400 invalid_payload
signals.review_reason: 主流程中发送图片数据直接返回 400 阻断错误，明确标注为 regression（回归问题），用户在 1.0.0 版本中图片上传功能完全不可用，属于关键功能不可用。

source_issues.title: Python: [Bug]: Content.from_uri regression - Service failed to complete the prompt: Error code: 400
source_issues.evidence: Using Content.from_uri with base64-encoded JPEG image data causes HTTP 400 error: {'error': {'code': 'invalid_payload', 'message': 'The provided data does not match the expected schema'}}. This is a regression in agent-framework 1.0.0 — the same code worked in prior versions. Users cannot send image data via base64, breaking multimodal input in FoundryChatClient.

signals.topic: Streaming mode aborts on OpenRouter/OpenAI — tool role message without preceding tool_calls triggers HTTP 400
signals.summary: 使用流式模式时，agent 工具调用后的下一步流式调用返回 HTTP 400，提示 tool role 消息必须跟随带有 tool_calls 的 preceding message，导致流式执行流程反复中断
aliases: Streaming aborts after tool call with OpenRouter 400
tool role message ordering bug in streaming
signals.review_reason: 流式执行主流程在工具调用后反复中止（HTTP 400），导致完整 agent 任务失败。有完整堆栈跟踪，错误根源在 OpenAIChatClient 流式路径的消息序列处理，属于主流程阻断。

source_issues.title: Python: [Bug]: Streaming fails with OpenRouter 400: tool role without preceding tool_calls
source_issues.evidence: Streaming agent execution fails after a tool call with OpenRouter returning HTTP 400: 'messages with role tool must be a response to a preceeding message with tool_calls'. The failure is wrapped by agent_framework_openai._chat_client.OpenAIChatClient and results in ChatClientException. Task fails and streaming aborts. This affects any streaming workflow that involves tool use.

signals.topic: FoundryAgent returns HTTP 400 when both agent_reference and tools are present in request body
signals.summary: FoundryAgent 同时传入 agent_reference 和 tools 参数时，序列化请求中包含 tools 导致 Foundry API 返回 400 错误，阻断用户在有 server-side 工具定义的 agent 上叠加本地工具实现的场景
aliases: FoundryAgent tools parameter conflicts with agent_reference causing 400
_prepare_options does not strip tools when agent_reference is present
signals.review_reason: FoundryAgent 核心使用场景（将 server-side agent 与本地工具实现结合）因 HTTP 400 完全阻断。_prepare_options 未在序列化时去除 tools 参数是明确的代码缺陷，企业级扩展场景不可用。

source_issues.title: Python: FoundryAgent returns 400 if both agent_reference and tools are present in request body
source_issues.evidence: FoundryAgent._prepare_options() validates FunctionTool objects but does not strip them from serialized request. When agent_reference is present, Foundry API rejects the request with 400: 'Not allowed when agent is specified' on param 'tools'. Users cannot override/extend server-side agent tools with local implementations — a valid enterprise use case is completely blocked.

signals.topic: LocalCommandLineCodeExecutor executes LLM-generated code on host without sandboxing — risk of credential theft and system compromise
signals.summary: The LocalCommandLineCodeExecutor writes LLM-generated code to disk and runs it as a subprocess with full host privileges. A UserWarning is emitted at init but is easily suppressed in production (e.g., -W ignore, filtered logs). An agent processing untrusted input can be tricked via indirect prompt injection into executing arbitrary code, leading to credential theft (SSH keys, cloud tokens), lateral movement, and data destruction.
signals.review_reason: This is a documented runtime security vulnerability with a concrete attack scenario. The LocalCommandLineCodeExecutor executes untrusted LLM-generated code as a host subprocess with no sandbox, filesystem isolation, or network restriction — only a suppressible UserWarning. Attackers can exploit indirect prompt injection to steal credentials (SSH keys, cloud tokens), move laterally, or destroy data. While count=1, the user impact evidence is explicit and severe (full system compromise, credential theft, lateral movement), meeting the P0 threshold for a single high-severity issue with a reproducible attack path.

source_issues.title: [Security] LocalCommandLineCodeExecutor executes LLM-generated code without sandboxing
source_issues.evidence: Attack scenario documented: agent processing untrusted data (user messages, web content, documents) is tricked via indirect prompt injection into generating malicious code that exfiltrates ~/.ssh/id_rsa and executes arbitrary commands with full host privileges. Only a UserWarning (silently suppressible) exists as safeguard. Cited by OWASP ASI-09 (Improper Output Handling) and CWE-94.

signals.topic: MCP server integrations lack fail-closed defaults — untrusted servers can execute unsafe tools by default
signals.summary: Users connecting AutoGen to MCP servers (documented in examples and quickstarts) face no runtime enforcement of trust boundaries. README documentation warns to only use trusted MCP servers, but the runtime has no hard enforcement — users can accidentally connect to untrusted or compromised MCP servers and have unsafe tools execute without explicit opt-in.
aliases: MCP server trust boundaries not enforced
signals.review_reason: This is a real architectural gap confirmed by a maintainer (davidahmann): MCP server integrations have no runtime trust enforcement, relying solely on documentation warnings that users routinely ignore or overlook. While not a single catastrophic attack, the user impact is systemic — any user following example code or connecting an MCP server without careful configuration is exposed. The fail-open default means the first-time or production user experience is fundamentally unsafe by default.

source_issues.title: Enforce fail-closed defaults for untrusted MCP server integrations
source_issues.evidence: Maintainer-raised issue (davidahmann) explicitly states: 'Example MCP integrations can be used in permissive ways without explicit trust boundaries, risking unsafe tool execution.' Current behavior: 'Safety relies on user discipline/documentation rather than hard fail-closed defaults.' Codepaths identified in autogen-ext and autogen-agentchat. Acceptance criteria: untrusted MCP configs should be rejected by default.

signals.topic: Multi-agent delegation chains inherit caller permissions without capability attenuation — risk of privilege escalation
signals.summary: When Agent A delegates a subtask to Agent B, and Agent B calls a tool, there is no mechanism to attenuate Agent A's full permission set. The delegated agent can invoke any tool the orchestrator could call. This maps to OWASP ASI04 (Privilege Escalation) and ASI06 (Excessive Agency). No capability scoping exists in current GroupChat or Swarm patterns.
signals.review_reason: This describes a real architectural gap in AutoGen's multi-agent delegation model: delegated agents inherit the full permission set of the delegator with no attenuation mechanism. The concrete attack scenario (a code-review agent that should only read files gaining write and external-API access through delegation) is well-defined and maps to recognized OWASP Agentic Security categories. While framed as a feature proposal, it identifies a structural gap in AutoGen's existing GroupChat/Swarm patterns that creates excessive-privilege risk in real multi-agent pipelines.

source_issues.title: Proposal: Capability-scoped tool authorization for AutoGen multi-agent pipelines
source_issues.evidence: Concrete delegation scenario documented: Orchestrator (has: read_files, write_files, call_external_api) delegates to CodeReviewAgent, which calls file_write('malicious_output.py'). Without capability scoping, the CodeReviewAgent inherits full orchestrator permissions. Referenced OWASP ASI04 and ASI06. The issue explicitly asks whether AutoGen has existing guardrails for inter-agent permission inheritance — the answer implied is no.

signals.topic: MCP tool inputSchema includes $schema field causing all Anthropic API tool calls to fail
signals.summary: Playwright MCP server generates tool schemas containing a top-level $schema field, which Anthropic API rejects with HTTP 400. Critically, one bad tool schema breaks ALL tool calls in the session, not just the affected tool, completely blocking MCP-based automation workflows.
signals.review_reason: Two related MCP issues: #40043 causes all Anthropic API tool calls to hard-fail with 400 errors (one bad schema kills the entire session), and #40018 causes stale backend state after disconnect. Together they make the MCP server unreliable for any production automation workflow. Confirmed user impact with specific API error messages.

source_issues.title: MCP: tool inputSchema includes $schema field, causing Anthropic API 400 errors
source_issues.evidence: Anthropic API returns 400 error: 'tools.N.custom.input_schema: JSON schema is invalid'. One invalid tool schema breaks ALL tool calls in the session. Affects mcp-remote, Claude Code, Claude Desktop, and any client forwarding schemas to Anthropic API.

source_issues.title: [MCP] backendPromise not cleared in onClose causes stale backend after disconnect
source_issues.evidence: When MCP server's onClose fires (browser or extension disconnect), backendPromise is not cleared, causing subsequent tool calls to await stale disposed backend and receive 'Not connected' errors.

signals.topic: Playwright v1.59.0 regression causes locator tests to timeout and fail

signals.topic: /responses endpoint silently hangs 10-28% of concurrent requests with no error/retry

Affected requests receive no HTTP error, no timeout, and no SDK retry — TCP connections hang indefinitely. Both raw AsyncOpenAI client and Agents SDK are affected at the same rate, confirming server-side root cause. This causes production request loss with no detection mechanism.
aliases: TCP connection hang on concurrent load

Confirmed reproducible across multiple runs and model versions. Not an SDK bug but directly blocks SDK users in production.

source_issues.evidence: 10-28% silent hang rate under concurrent load across 4 test runs. No HTTP response, no timeout, no SDK retry. Reproducible across gpt-5.1 and gpt-5.4-2026-03-05. Raw client and SDK affected at same rate.

signals.topic: Agent loop runaway causes uncontrolled API call explosion and cost overrun
