Current examples and documentation focus on building agents but provide no guidance on pre-deployment safety checks, cost controls, or fallback behavior.
signals.review_reason: Real cost loss incident documented (thousands of unexpected API calls). The SDK provides no built-in cost limits or runaway detection, placing full financial risk on users. This is a production deployment blocker for cost-sensitive applications.

source_issues.title: How are you handling cost / safety checks before deploying agents?
source_issues.evidence: User reports an agent loop triggered thousands of API calls unexpectedly, causing significant cost overrun. No built-in cost limits or safety checks exist in the SDK.

signals.topic: RedisSession blocks event loop, breaking streaming in production
signals.summary: When using RedisSession with Runner.run_streamed() on production platforms (FastAPI on Heroku with TLS Redis), streaming events are never produced. The first Redis call appears to block the event loop before the producer task can emit events. With session=None, streaming works correctly. This breaks the primary streaming use case in production environments.
aliases: run_streamed hangs with RedisSession on Heroku
signals.review_reason: Production streaming is completely broken when using RedisSession. The stream never starts — no events emitted — making streaming unusable in Redis-backed production deployments. Reproducible on Heroku with TLS Redis; working with session=None confirms RedisSession as root cause.

source_issues.title: Using redis to preserve chat sessions in prod
source_issues.evidence: run_streamed returns immediately with no events produced when session=RedisSession. With session=None, events stream correctly. Suspected synchronous Redis I/O blocking the event loop on Heroku with TLS.

signals.topic: Traces silently dropped in long-running workers (Celery, FastAPI background tasks)

Long-running workers that never restart accumulate buffered traces indefinitely with no warning, no error, and no indication to users that their traces are lost.
aliases: BatchTraceProcessor silent trace loss in background workers
tracing not appearing dashboard Celery FastAPI
signals.review_reason: Complete silent failure of a key observability feature in production worker environments. Traces are created (IDs visible in logs) but permanently lost with zero feedback. Affects all major async worker frameworks. No warning emitted makes this extremely hard to diagnose.

source_issues.title: Traces are silently dropped in long-running workers
source_issues.evidence: Traces never reach platform.openai.com/traces in Celery tasks and FastAPI background tasks. BatchTraceProcessor only flushes on shutdown. No error or warning emitted. Affects all major background task frameworks.

signals.topic: No public rewind/retry/edit API for chat sessions — forces fragile manual history manipulation
signals.summary: Users building chat applications with persistent sessions have no built-in way to delete, retry, or edit the last user message. The existing rewind_input is an internal retry mechanism for locked conversations, not a public undo API. Users must manually walk backward through flat item lists to find message boundaries, which breaks in multi-agent handoffs and cross-turn tool call scenarios. Google ADK exposes this as a first-class rewind_async API; the OpenAI SDK lacks any equivalent.
aliases: no rewind undo API for conversation sessions
lack of turn-level undo in session management
signals.review_reason: Missing core UX feature for chat applications forces fragile manual workarounds. The fragility is demonstrated by the specific failure case: manual history manipulation breaks with multi-agent handoffs and cross-turn tool calls. A competitive SDK (Google ADK) already provides this as first-class functionality.

source_issues.title: Best strategy for delete / retry / edit last user message (rewind equivalent)
source_issues.evidence: No public rewind/undo API for sessions. Users must manually manipulate flat item lists. Existing rewind_input is internal-only. Comparison with Google ADK's first-class rewind_async API highlights SDK gap.

signals.review_reason: Explicit cost impact documented (API credits wasted) plus time loss. The --session flag silently producing wrong behavior (one-shot instead of session mode) is a UX footgun with financial and efficiency consequences. Count=1 but high confidence due to explicit credit/cost evidence in issue body.

source_issues.title: CLI command structure is extremely confusing for AI agents — acpx claude vs acpx claude prompt vs acpx claude exec
source_issues.evidence: AI agent used wrong CLI syntax 3 times consecutively, each time wasting API credits and user time. --session flag on top-level command silently ignored in exec mode — looks like session mode but runs one-shot. User explicitly reports: 'Each mistake wastes my user's time and API credits.' Clear cost impact for AI agent workflows.

signals.topic: `--no-wait` fire-and-forget queue submission loses jobs — prompt never processed
signals.summary: When using `--no-wait` to submit a fire-and-forget prompt, the job is queued but the queue owner never processes it. The queue owner process stays alive and responsive to regular prompts, but jobs submitted via the IPC queue with `--no-wait` are silently lost. Only `--timeout` workaround is available, which blocks instead of being truly fire-and-forget.
signals.review_reason: Documented job loss (fire-and-forget silently fails) with clear repro steps. The queue owner is alive and responsive to regular prompts, so this is a specific bug in how the IPC queue path handles --no-wait submissions. Impact is job loss rather than workflow blocking, hence P2 rather than P0/P1. keep=true because there is a clear repro and the queued job is genuinely lost (not just delayed).

source_issues.title: [BUG] --no-wait queues prompt but queue owner never processes it
source_issues.evidence: Using --no-wait: command returns '[queued] <job-id>' immediately but the file is never created. Queue owner is alive and responsive to regular prompts, but jobs submitted via IPC queue with --no-wait are silently lost with no error. User must use --timeout workaround which blocks instead of fire-and-forget.

signals.topic: Security scanner incorrectly flags legitimate skills as suspicious — network call heuristics trigger false positives
signals.summary: The ClawHub automated security scanner generates false positive suspicious flags on multiple legitimate skills (Spotify agent, Solana token monitor, Feishu bot, VMware log tools, game monitors, file converters, etc.) due to over-broad heuristics targeting outbound network calls, file writes, and external API access. Multiple skill publishers have filed appeals with no resolution, blocking skill discovery and use.
aliases: false positive security flags on skills
signals.review_reason: High volume of distinct publishers (13+ separate skill authors, 16 total suspicious-flag-related issues) reporting false positive security flags is a systemic workflow failure in the ClawHub skill publishing pipeline. Legitimate skills across diverse domains (finance, productivity, developer tools, gaming) are blocked from the marketplace due to over-broad scanner heuristics. Multiple publishers explicitly state they cannot identify which rule triggered the flag or how to fix it, indicating the scanner provides no actionable feedback. While each false positive affects individual skill authors, the cumulative pattern directly degrades the skill ecosystem's diversity and completeness — a core platform value proposition.

source_issues.title: Skill flagged suspicious, scan tagged benign
source_issues.evidence: Spotify agent skill flagged suspicious, but the scan itself tagged it benign. Direct contradiction between flag and scan result.

source_issues.title: False positive: solana-token-monitor flagged as suspicious — legitimate public API calls
source_issues.evidence: Skill only calls DexScreener public API (read-only). Outbound HTTP to crypto domains pattern-matches malicious heuristics incorrectly.

source_issues.title: False positive: TrencherAI skill flagged for undeclared credentials
source_issues.evidence: Coinbase CDP code example with apiKeyId/apiKeySecret references incorrectly flagged as credential exfiltration. These are client's own credentials, not exfiltrated data.

source_issues.title: feishu-quick-setup skill incorrectly flagged as suspicious
source_issues.evidence: Official Feishu API calls, file writes to config, process.exit — all standard patterns flagged incorrectly. Publisher cannot identify which rule triggered the flag.

source_issues.title: False Positive Security Flag for VCF Log Insight Skill
source_issues.evidence: Skill uses curl with Bearer token to user's own VMware environment. Scanner flagged it as potential data exfiltration or malicious shell execution incorrectly.

source_issues.title: False positive suspicious flag on emotion-shared-experience skill
source_issues.evidence: Fully local skill — no network, no external calls, only local JSON file reads/writes. Still flagged due to automatic directory creation.

source_issues.title: False positive suspicious flag on blindoracle — metadata mismatch + crypto terminology
source_issues.evidence: Legitimate DeFi terms (x402, Fedimint, ecash) flagged as crypto-scam heuristics. Also metadata extraction bug causes false undeclared-env-vars flag.

source_issues.title: wangqianqianjun/eps — flagged suspicious
source_issues.evidence: EPS to SVG/PDF/JPG/PNG conversion service — no user data retained, no malicious behavior.

source_issues.title: evolution-whatsapp — flagged suspicious
source_issues.evidence: WhatsApp integration skill incorrectly flagged with no further details provided by reporter.

source_issues.title: game-sentiment flagged as suspicious
source_issues.evidence: First-time publisher; pure game monitor skill incorrectly flagged as suspicious.

source_issues.title: agent-see flagged
source_issues.evidence: Legitimate skill incorrectly flagged as suspicious.

source_issues.title: fit-converter skill flagged as suspicious
source_issues.evidence: Official FIT file converter skill — an officially supported skill in the ecosystem — incorrectly flagged. Publisher cannot identify what triggered the flag.

source_issues.title: Re-scan jarviyin/clawpk v5.0.0 — remove suspicious flag
source_issues.evidence: Skill restructured entirely — removed index.js, uses wallet signature verification, still flagged from previous version's metadata.

signals.topic: Security scanner flags legitimate skills using fs.readFileSync/writeFileSync for core file operations
signals.summary: Legitimate skills that require filesystem access for core functionality (e.g., German text corrector, emotion memory storage) are incorrectly flagged as suspicious due to fs module usage, despite these being essential, non-malicious operations with no network access or code execution.
signals.review_reason: The fs module false positive has been reported twice by distinct publishers with completely different use cases (text processing and emotion memory), indicating it is a recurring scanner rule issue rather than isolated cases. The humanizer-de report explicitly notes that previous versions (v1.1.0 and v1.1.1) passed the scan without flagging, suggesting a scanner rule regression. This blocks legitimate file-manipulation skills from being published.

source_issues.title: False positive: humanizer-de v1.1.2 flagged as suspicious (fs.readFileSync/writeFileSync for text correction)
source_issues.evidence: German AI-text corrector uses fs.readFileSync/writeFileSync as core feature (read text, create .bak backup, write corrected file). No network access, no exec, no eval. Previous versions passed scan; v1.1.2 was flagged without code changes to fs usage.

source_issues.title: False positive suspicious flag on emotion-shared-experience skill
source_issues.evidence: Fully local emotion memory skill; fs operations only. Directory auto-creation triggered the flag despite no malicious behavior.

signals.topic: Safari (WebKit/JavaScriptCore) users cannot access clawhub.ai website — SyntaxError causes complete site breakdown
signals.summary: The ClawHub website throws an unhandled SyntaxError in Safari/WebKit due to the `return x in y` pattern being misinterpreted by JavaScriptCore, making the entire site unusable for Safari users. Multiple users have confirmed the issue across different macOS Safari installations; the website functionality is completely blocked.
signals.review_reason: This is a primary-flow-blocking issue. Safari users (non-trivial segment of macOS users) cannot access the ClawHub website at all due to a JavaScriptCore parser bug triggered by the `return x in y` syntax pattern. The issue is confirmed across multiple installations and the reporter explicitly states website functionality is 'completely blocked.' This is a clear P0 — a core platform (the website) is unusable for an entire browser engine.

source_issues.title: Safari (WebKit/JavaScriptCore) SyntaxError: Unexpected keyword 'in' on website pages
source_issues.evidence: Unhandled Promise Rejection: SyntaxError: Unexpected keyword 'in'. Expected a ';' following a return statement. Confirmed on multiple macOS Safari installations. Website functionality is completely blocked as a result.

signals.topic: GitHub OAuth login flow completes 302 redirect but fails to create authenticated session — users remain logged out
signals.summary: Users attempting to log in via GitHub OAuth encounter a silent failure where the OAuth callback returns 302 successfully but no session cookie is created, leaving them logged out with no error message shown. Suspected root cause is a stale/soft-deleted user or OAuth mapping conflict from a previously deleted account.
signals.review_reason: This is an auth-flow issue that silently blocks user login via GitHub OAuth. The OAuth exchange completes without visible errors, but the session is never created, leaving users stuck in a logged-out state. The silent nature (no error surfaced to UI) makes it particularly confusing and disruptive. While only one issue is reported, the auth path is a primary platform flow and the silent failure pattern is a distinct UX anti-pattern.

source_issues.title: GitHub OAuth callback succeeds (302) but no session is created
source_issues.evidence: OAuth code exchange appears successful (302 redirect to /), but no session cookie is set and user remains logged out. Failure happens at user lookup/session creation stage. No error is surfaced to the UI, making this a silent auth failure that blocks the primary login flow.

signals.topic: ClawHub dashboard becomes inaccessible — ErrorBoundary crash on Publisher Dashboard page
signals.summary: The ClawHub dashboard throws a React ErrorBoundary catch error ('React.Children.only expected to receive a single React element child') and renders a blank/error page, making the Publisher Dashboard inaccessible. Users cannot manage their published skills or view dashboard analytics.
aliases: ErrorBoundary caught React error on dashboard
signals.review_reason: A React ErrorBoundary crash on the Publisher Dashboard renders the page inaccessible, blocking publishers from managing their skills. This is a critical path for skill creators. The crash is a clear regression that causes a key platform feature to be unavailable.

source_issues.title: clawhub dashboard is unavailable
source_issues.evidence: ErrorBoundary caught: Error: React.Children.only expected to receive a single React element child. Dashboard is unavailable — users cannot access the Publisher Dashboard.

signals.topic: Parser mishandles escaped characters in quoted args, breaking --args-json payloads
signals.summary: The lobster workflow parser corrupts --args-json payloads containing escaped apostrophes or complex JSON escape sequences, causing parse failures or silent data corruption. This breaks pipelines that pass prompt-rich JSON through --args-json, especially when prompts contain apostrophes or newlines.
aliases: Single-quoted args with apostrophes cause parse failure
signals.review_reason: This is a real parser bug with documented failure modes: (1) escaped apostrophes in single-quoted JSON throw 'Unclosed quote', and (2) escape sequences in double-quoted JSON are altered, corrupting payload semantics. It blocks workflows that pass natural-language prompts containing apostrophes or newlines via --args-json, directly breaking execution. Explicit reproduction steps and error outputs are provided. Count=1 but severity is high due to direct execution-blocking nature.

source_issues.title: Parser mishandles escaped characters in quoted args, breaking --args-json payloads
source_issues.evidence: Issue #17: parsePipeline/tokenizeCommand mishandles escapes inside quoted arguments. Backslashes in double-quoted args alter JSON content; escaped apostrophes in single-quoted args are treated as quote terminators, throwing 'Unclosed quote'. This breaks existing pipelines that pass prompt-rich JSON through --args-json, especially payloads containing apostrophes and escaped characters.

signals.topic: Approval tokens too long for chat-surface inline buttons, breaking human-in-the-loop on Telegram and Discord
signals.summary: Lobster approval gates generate base64-encoded JWT-style resume tokens (~150+ chars) that exceed the inline button payload limits of Telegram (64 bytes) and Discord (100 chars). This breaks the core human-in-the-loop mechanism on the two most popular chat surfaces, forcing users to copy-paste long tokens instead of one-tap approval.
aliases: Long approval tokens incompatible with Telegram/Discord buttons
Approval gates not actionable on chat platforms
Approval tokens exceed platform button payload limits
signals.review_reason: This is a genuine user pain point: approval tokens (the core human-in-the-loop mechanism) cannot be presented as one-tap buttons on Telegram and Discord due to platform payload limits. The issue documents explicit platform compatibility table (Telegram: 64 bytes, Discord: 100 chars, both insufficient for ~150+ char tokens), describes a brittle two-step workaround the team is currently using, and states the mechanism is broken on the two most popular chat surfaces. While count=1, the evidence clearly shows a repeated, user-visible degradation of a core feature.

source_issues.title: Approval tokens too long for chat-surface buttons (Telegram, Discord)
source_issues.evidence: Issue #46: Lobster approval gates generate ~150+ char base64 JWT resume tokens that exceed Telegram's 64-byte and Discord's 100-char inline button limits. The author documents a brittle two-step workaround: a hardcoded '/restart' callback that triggers lobster resume on the backend. The issue explicitly states 'approval gates — the core human-in-the-loop mechanism — cannot be presented as one-tap buttons on the two most popular chat surfaces', forcing users to copy-paste long tokens from text messages.

signals.topic: Windows: `ollama launch openclaw` creates duplicate gateway when Scheduled Task is already running (Session 0 isolation)
signals.summary: When the OpenClaw Gateway runs as a Windows Scheduled Task in Session 0, `ollama launch openclaw` cannot detect it via standard process enumeration, spawning a second node.exe that binds to the same port 18789. This causes port conflicts, mDNS name conflicts, EPERM file lock errors, and full handshake failures — completely blocking remote connectivity.
signals.review_reason: 主流程阻断：用户无法通过 `ollama launch openclaw` 正常启动，重复进程导致端口冲突、文件锁竞争、mDNS 冲突、WebSocket 握手失败，远程连接功能完全不可用。症状覆盖主流程多个环节，影响明确且无自动恢复。

source_issues.title: [Windows] ollama launch openclaw starts duplicate gateway when Scheduled Task is already running
source_issues.evidence: User reported: two LISTENING entries on port 18789, mDNS renamed to '(2)', 'RPC probe: failed', EPERM writing to pending.json, mass handshake timeout / gateway closed (1006) errors. Root cause: Session 0 process invisible to user session via standard enumeration.

signals.topic: Windows Tray App: node stays permanently disconnected after Gateway restart, no auto-reconnect
signals.summary: When the OpenClaw Gateway restarts, the Windows Tray App node mode does not automatically reconnect. The node stays in a permanently disconnected state indefinitely, with no retry logic — unlike the CLI node which does retry. Manual workaround required: toggle Node Mode off/on in settings.
aliases: Tray App node disconnect on gateway restart
Node Mode auto-reconnect missing in Tray App
signals.review_reason: 节点关键功能不可用：Tray App 的 Node Mode 在 Gateway 重启后永久断开，无自动重连逻辑，用户必须手动操作才能恢复。与 CLI node 的行为不一致，关键功能降级严重，虽非主流程阻断但影响核心节点连接能力。

source_issues.title: Windows Tray App does not auto-reconnect after Gateway restart
source_issues.evidence: User reported: after Gateway restart, Tray App shows '[INFO] Node status changed: Disconnected' with no reconnection attempts logged. CLI node correctly retries but Tray App does not. Workaround requires manually toggling Node Mode off/on. Gateway: remote WSS over Nginx TLS proxy. Version 0.4.7.

signals.topic: SSH tunnel process unexpected exit leaves remote connectivity broken with no automatic restart
signals.summary: When the SSH tunnel process exits unexpectedly, SshTunnelService only logs a warning without cleaning up internal state (_process/_lastSpec) or raising any event. The gateway client keeps reconnecting to an unreachable localhost port in an infinite loop, leaving remote connectivity broken until the user manually intervenes.
aliases: SSH tunnel crash leaves dangling connection
SshTunnelService Exited handler missing cleanup and restart
SSH tunnel silent failure no recovery
signals.review_reason: 关键功能不可用且无自动恢复：SSH 隧道意外退出后无任何清理和重启机制，客户端陷入对已死亡端口的无限重连循环，远程连接功能完全失效，需用户手动干预。与 pp-2 类似，属于连接失败后缺少自动恢复逻辑的系统性问题。

source_issues.title: Bug: SSH tunnel not restarted on unexpected exit
source_issues.evidence: Identified in code review: process.Exited handler (~lines 123-134) only logs warning, does not null _process/_lastSpec, does not raise event, does not attempt restart. Gateway client spins forever reconnecting to dead localhost port. Manual intervention required (change settings or restart app).

signals.topic: Signature mode fallback gets permanently stuck if initial mode is rejected — never retries with fallback mode
signals.summary: When the gateway rejects a device signature with 'device signature invalid', HandleRequestError advances _signatureTokenMode to the next fallback mode but never re-sends the connect message. The client stays permanently stuck in Connecting state with the WebSocket open but unauthenticated. The fallback mode only takes effect if a full reconnect cycle occurs.
aliases: client stuck in Connecting state after signature rejection
device signature invalid fallback never retried
signals.review_reason: 认证流程阻断：签名模式被拒绝后客户端永久卡在 Connecting 状态，WebSocket 打开但未认证，fallback 模式永不生效。这是主认证流程的严重缺陷，导致设备在签名模式切换场景下完全无法连接，与 pp-2/pp-3 同属连接失败后缺少正确恢复逻辑。

source_issues.title: Bug: Signature mode fallback never retries connect message
source_issues.evidence: Identified in code review: HandleRequestError (~lines 776-796) advances signature mode but does not re-send SendConnectMessageAsync. Client permanently stuck in Connecting state if initial signature mode is rejected (clock skew, key mismatch). Fallback mode only activates on full reconnect cycle which may never occur.

signals.topic: Model fallback chain fails to activate on primary provider errors, causing indefinite retry loops or missed fallbacks
signals.summary: OpenClaw fails to invoke configured model fallback chains when primary providers return errors, leading to indefinite retry loops or false success signals on failed fallbacks. Affects both Anthropic 503 (overloaded_error) and fallback candidates returning 404.
signals.review_reason: Primary model unavailability is a core blocking scenario; both issues combine to show the fallback mechanism is comprehensively broken — either it never fires (62141) or it fires but declares failure as success (62119). Both lead to user-visible main flow failure with no automatic recovery.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: OpenClaw 2026.4.5 fails to fallback on Anthropic overloaded_error (503), retries indefinitely
source_issues.evidence: When Anthropic returns 503 (overloaded_error), OpenClaw retries the same provider indefinitely instead of attempting configured fallbacks (Gemini, OpenAI). Session times out. Known documented bug per #32533 and #49079, yet unfixed.

source_issues.title: Bug: model-fallback marks candidate_succeeded even when fallback model returns 404
source_issues.evidence: When a fallback candidate returns 404, OpenClaw logs candidate_succeeded and never attempts subsequent fallback candidates. User sees error instead of working fallback model. Logs show isError=true but decision=candidate_succeeded.

signals.topic: Gateway crashes with unhandled promise rejection in exec/PTY subsystem, requires manual restart
signals.summary: Gateway crashes intermittently when an exec/PTY background session emits stdout after the parent agent run has completed, causing an unhandled promise rejection that terminates the service.
aliases: agent listener outside active run crash
signals.review_reason: Service crashes are the most severe user impact — main gateway process terminates, blocking all active sessions and requiring manual intervention. Multiple occurrences in a single day with clear stack trace confirms this is not transient.

source_issues.title: Unhandled promise rejection: Agent listener invoked outside active run (exec/PTY)
source_issues.evidence: Gateway crashes multiple times in one day with 'Unhandled promise rejection: Error: Agent listener invoked outside active run'. systemd service stops unexpectedly, requiring manual restart each time. No automatic recovery.

signals.topic: openai-codex provider returns Cloudflare 403 on headless HTTP after upgrade to 2026.4.5, making primary Codex models unusable
signals.summary: After upgrading to 2026.4.5, the openai-codex provider consistently fails with Cloudflare 403 responses on the /codex/responses endpoint despite valid OAuth tokens, rendering gpt-5.4 and gpt-5.4-mini unusable.
signals.review_reason: Users selecting gpt-5.4 or gpt-5.4-mini as primary models experience complete workflow failure — zero successful requests. Upgrade-induced regression with explicit reproduction steps and curl confirmation proves this is a consistent, non-transient block.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: openai-codex provider fails with Cloudflare 403 on headless HTTP after upgrade to 2026.4.5
source_issues.evidence: Every request to chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex/responses returns 403 with Cloudflare HTML. Token verified valid against other endpoints. Regression after 2026.4.5 upgrade. gpt-5.4 and gpt-5.4-mini primary models completely unusable.

signals.topic: Multiple plugins fail to load on Node 24 due to Zod RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded
signals.summary: On Node 24, multiple bundled plugins fail to load at gateway startup with Zod throwing RangeError during JSON Schema/AJV validation compilation.
aliases: call stack size exceeded plugin loader
signals.review_reason: Plugin loading failure at startup blocks multiple provider integrations from functioning. Node 24 adoption is increasing; seven distinct plugins affected simultaneously means significant feature surface is unavailable. Explicitly labeled as regression.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: Zod RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded — Multiple plugins fail to load on Node 24
source_issues.evidence: Seven bundled plugins (minimax, amazon-bedrock, amazon-bedrock-mantle, google, kilocode, moonshot, comfy) fail to load at gateway startup on Node 24.14.1. Stack trace shows infinite recursion in zod/index.cjs during validation compilation. Regression from prior version.

signals.topic: 2026.4.5 post-update migration leaves gateway in partially broken state with token drift
signals.summary: After upgrading from 2026.3.x to 2026.4.5, the gateway can end up in a partially migrated state: Discord config keys rejected at startup, and launchd plist embeds a stale gateway token even though the running process correctly resolves it from SecretRef.
signals.review_reason: Post-upgrade state corruption is a main flow blocker: gateway cannot start without manual repair intervention. While affecting a single user here, upgrade-induced startup failure is a high-severity scenario that any upgrading user could encounter.

source_issues.title: 2026.4.5 post-update recovery can leave launchd gateway token drift after config migration repair
source_issues.evidence: Upgrade from 2026.3.31 to 2026.4.5 leaves gateway unable to start until openclaw doctor --fix runs. After fix, launchd plist still embeds stale token while running process uses correct SecretRef. Gateway must be manually reconfigured to recover fully.

signals.topic: stdin 输入导致内核中断，终止长时运行代码（Ctrl+C 无法正确处理）

aliases: kernel interrupted after stdin kills long-running code
signals.review_reason: 该 issue 描述了用户在使用 Open Interpreter 时，按下 Ctrl+C 或任何 stdin 输入会导致内核进程被中断，正在执行的长时代码任务（如数据分析、模型训练等）被强制终止。这直接导致用户工作丢失和主流程阻断，属于典型的工作流运行时痛点。虽然来源于自动化扫描，但其根因（stdin 与内核进程信号处理不当）有 PR #1455 对应，属于真实可复现的代码缺陷。

signals.topic: OpenAI 兼容端点允许远程客户端在未认证情况下切换 auto_run，可能导致未经授权的自动代码执行
signals.summary: OpenAI 兼容的 chat completion 端点接受消息内容中的 AUTO_RUN_ON 参数，在未设置 INTERPRETER_REQUIRE_AUTH 时，任何客户端均可远程启用 auto_run，绕过确认门禁，直接执行任意代码。
aliases: Remote auto_run enable via OpenAI-compatible endpoint unauthenticated
auto_run bypasses confirmation via message content
signals.review_reason: 该安全问题有明确的根因描述和验证路径：在默认配置（未设置 INTERPRETER_REQUIRE_AUTH）下，OpenAI 兼容端点解析消息内容中的 AUTO_RUN_ON 参数即可远程启用 auto_run，绕过确认门禁直接执行任意代码。这意味着在默认部署下，任何能访问该端点的客户端均可触发自动代码执行，是真实的安全影响。虽然来源于自动化扫描，但描述的是默认配置下的权限绕过，具有明确的安全含义，符合痛点中'关键功能不可用/滥用'维度。

source_issues.title: Qodo AntiSlop scan found 46 issues across 10 recent PRs
source_issues.evidence: 安全扫描确认：当 INTERPRETER_REQUIRE_AUTH 未设置时，OpenAI 兼容端点接受 {AUTO_RUN_ON} 参数可直接设置 async_interpreter.auto_run=True，绕过所有确认机制。默认配置下任何客户端均可远程触发自动代码执行。
