signals.topic: Windows cp1252 console encoding errors crash aider output
signals.summary: On Windows with cp1252 console encoding, certain Unicode characters (e.g., \u22ee vertical ellipsis) cannot be encoded, causing aider to crash with UnicodeEncodeError when printing repo-map or other structured output.
signals.review_reason: Two confirmed Windows users encounter an uncaught UnicodeEncodeError when the rich console tries to print Unicode characters to a cp1252-encoded Windows terminal. The crash propagates through io.tool_output, crashing aider during repo-map display. This is a blocking crash for affected Windows users. count=2 confirmed.

source_issues.title: Uncaught UnicodeEncodeError in cp1252.py line 19
source_issues.evidence: On Windows 11 with cp1252 console encoding, Unicode character \u22ee in console output causes UnicodeEncodeError: 'charmap' codec can't encode character. Crash occurs in rich console write_buffer -> legacy_windows_render, crashing during io.tool_output(repo_map).

source_issues.title: Uncaught UnicodeEncodeError in cp1252.py line 19
source_issues.evidence: Duplicate of #4986, same crash on Windows 11 cp1252 console. Same error: UnicodeEncodeError in _win32_console.py encode() when writing buffer. Confirms this is a recurring user-impacting crash on Windows.

signals.topic: Uncaught RuntimeError crash due to symlink loop in repo scan
signals.summary: When repo scan encounters a broken/circular symlink, Python's pathlib.resolve() throws an uncaught RuntimeError, crashing aider during repo-map generation. Blocks the main coding flow entirely.
aliases: Symlink loop crash during repo map
signals.review_reason: This is a real user-impacting crash: the app encounters a broken symlink in a user's repo and exits with an uncaught RuntimeError, blocking the entire coding session. The error propagates from pathlib.resolve() through the repo-map path and is never caught. Multiple users are affected across different environments (Linux/WSL).

source_issues.title: Uncaught RuntimeError in pathlib.py line 1237
source_issues.evidence: Symlink loop at '/home/user/git/dotfiles/nvim/.config/nvim/vim' causes RuntimeError: 'Symlink loop from...' to propagate uncaught through get_repo_map -> format_messages -> run_one, crashing aider at startup/repo-scan. Main flow completely blocked.

signals.topic: Uncaught OSError due to over-long file paths crashing aider startup
signals.summary: When a file path (often from --system-message arguments) exceeds OS limits, pathlib.is_dir() raises an uncaught OSError (Errno 36: File name too long), crashing aider before any user interaction occurs.
aliases: File name too long OSError startup crash
signals.review_reason: A user passes a long --system-message argument, and aider crashes immediately at startup with an uncaught OSError. This blocks the entire user session before any productive work can begin. The crash is reproducible and clearly blocks the main flow.

source_issues.title: Uncaught OSError in pathlib.py line 842
source_issues.evidence: OSError [Errno 36] File name too long triggered from a --system-message argument, causing aider to crash at main.py line 704 before any user interaction. The crash occurs in pathlib.is_dir() call during argument validation.

signals.topic: PermissionError when cache directory is not writable, blocking startup
signals.summary: Aider attempts to create a cache directory at /app/.aider/caches but encounters PermissionError, causing aider to crash on startup before any coding activity.
aliases: Permission denied cache directory startup crash
signals.review_reason: Users in containerized or restricted environments encounter a PermissionError when aider tries to create its cache directory. The crash occurs before the interactive session starts, completely blocking use. Issue was closed but the underlying permission handling gap in the startup path remains.

source_issues.title: Uncaught PermissionError in pathlib.py line 1311
source_issues.evidence: PermissionError [Errno 13] Permission denied for '/app/.aider/caches' triggers at versioncheck.py line 94 when attempting to mkdir, crashing aider before the user can begin any coding session. Affects container/Docker environments.

signals.topic: LLM model fails edit format causing frequent rejected edits
signals.summary: Users attempting to use mistral/mistral-small-2603 receive 'LLM did not conform to the edit format' errors, meaning the model output cannot be applied and the edit workflow is blocked.
signals.review_reason: Users relying on specific models (mistral-small-2603) experience repeated edit rejections, preventing them from completing code modification tasks. This is a workflow-blocking issue for affected model users, though the count is currently 1.

source_issues.title: Support mistral/mistral-small-2603
source_issues.evidence: User explicitly reports that with mistral/mistral-small-2603 model, edits are rejected with 'The LLM did not conform to the edit format' — this blocks the primary edit workflow for users relying on this model.

signals.topic: Installation/redteam运行时出现ERR_REQUIRE_ASYNC_MODULE错误导致主流程阻断
signals.summary: 用户在Node.js 22.21.1环境下运行npx promptfoo@latest redteam eval时，触发ERR_REQUIRE_ASYNC_MODULE错误，应用直接崩溃退出，无法完成红队评估任务。
signals.review_reason: 主流程阻断性崩溃：用户在真实环境中运行核心功能（redteam eval）时应用直接抛出未捕获异常退出，Node.js ESM异步模块加载失败导致redteaming任务完全无法进行，属于高严重性的主流程阻断问题。

source_issues.title: Unable to install latest version of promptfoo
source_issues.evidence: 运行npx promptfoo@latest redteam eval时直接抛出ERR_REQUIRE_ASYNC_MODULE异常，进程崩溃退出，主流程完全阻断。用户提供完整堆栈信息。

signals.topic: crossSessionLeak grader在metadata缺失时将undefined当作字符串搜索，导致安全检测静默失效
signals.summary: crossSessionLeak grader当test.metadata.crossSessionLeakMatch未配置时，会将undefined强制转换为字符串"undefined"进行includes搜索，导致含有undefined词汇的正常输出被误判为泄露，同时metadata缺失时实际泄露也被漏检——安全功能完全静默失效。
aliases: security test false positive false negative
signals.review_reason: 安全功能静默失效：crossSessionLeak是promptfoo红队安全检测的核心功能，当metadata缺失时同时产生误报（false positive）和漏报（false negative），导致安全评估结果不可信，属于关键安全功能不可用。

source_issues.title: bug: crossSessionLeak grader silently searches for string "undefined" when metadata is missing
source_issues.evidence: 代码在src/redteam/plugins/crossSessionLeak.ts:155-156处直接对undefined调用includes()，JS将其强制转换为字符串"undefined"搜索，导致正常输出被误判；同时配置缺失时grader总是pass，安全检测静默失效。

signals.topic: not-javascript断言类型在value为特定类型时无法正确取反
signals.summary: assertion type 'not-javascript'在value类型为number、function、object时无法正确取反，导致用户期望失败的测试反而通过，断言验证逻辑不可靠。
signals.review_reason: 断言验证逻辑缺陷：not-javascript的inverse功能在多个value类型上不可用，导致用户测试中的安全检查（期望输出不含JS代码）无法正确失败，关键验证功能不可靠。

source_issues.title: assertion type: "not-javascript" doesn't work in all cases
source_issues.evidence: 用户报告type: not-javascript与value: (o,c)=>true组合时期望失败但实际通过，handleJavascript()函数仅在value为boolean时处理inverse，其他类型（number/function/object）的inverse分支缺失。

signals.topic: apiKeyRequired配置对anthropic:claude-agent-sdk不生效
signals.summary: 用户配置apiKeyRequired: false后仍然收到Missing ANTHROPIC_API_KEY错误，导致使用Claude订阅（非API key）的用户无法在promptfoo中使用claude-agent-sdkprovider。
aliases: apiKeyRequired not respected for anthropic provider
signals.review_reason: 关键配置项失效：apiKeyRequired功能对重要provider(anthropic:claude-agent-sdk)不生效，阻止了使用Claude订阅而非API key的用户群体使用核心功能，属于关键功能不可用。

source_issues.title: apiKeyRequired not working for anthropic:claude-agent-sdk
source_issues.evidence: 用户在yaml中正确配置了apiKeyRequired: false但运行时仍报Missing ANTHROPIC_API_KEY错误，阻断使用Claude订阅版provider的主要用例。

signals.topic: 嵌入TypeScript前端项目时报TypeScript enum strip-only模式不支持错误
signals.summary: 用户将promptfoo作为库嵌入到TypeScript前端项目时，运行npx promptfoo eval报错'TypeScript enum is not supported in strip-only mode'，尝试NODE_OPTIONS转换类型后报模块找不到错误，主流程完全阻断。
aliases: TypeScript enum strip-only error in node package
embedding promptfoo in TypeScript project fails
signals.review_reason: 库嵌入场景阻断：用户尝试将promptfoo作为node包集成到已有TypeScript项目时报错且无有效解决方案，主流程eval命令无法执行，属于关键集成场景不可用。

source_issues.title: Integrating Promptfoo with a Frontend TypeScript Project
source_issues.evidence: 用户将promptfoo作为node package嵌入已有TypeScript项目后运行eval报错TypeScript enum not supported，workaround尝试也失败，主流程阻断。

signals.topic: MCP tool integration lacks cryptographic identity, message signing, and integrity verification — enabling tool poisoning and message tampering
signals.summary: Three independent reports identify that the MCP integration has no agent identity certificates, no message signing for JSON-RPC calls, no tool definition integrity checks, and no replay protection. OWASP MCP Top 10 classifies tool poisoning (MCP03) as a known attack vector.
signals.review_reason: Three independent issues converge on the same root cause: the MCP integration has no authentication or integrity layer. This enables OWASP-documented tool poisoning (MCP03) and man-in-the-middle message tampering. Count=3 meets the P0 frequency threshold, and the security implications with OWASP attribution constitute a high-severity user impact — agents cannot safely be deployed in regulated or production environments.

source_issues.title: MCP tool integration has no per-message authentication or integrity verification
source_issues.evidence: No agent passport/certificate, unsigned JSON-RPC messages, no tool definition signing, no replay protection. OWASP MCP Top 10 cited as reference.

source_issues.title: Proposal: Native Verification Receipts via Apache-2.0 Acta Protocol
source_issues.evidence: MCP has no built-in access control, rate limiting, audit trail, or identity gating. Author built protect-mcp as a workaround, requesting native LlamaIndex support.

source_issues.title: Feature: Agent Identity & Trust Verification for LlamaIndex Agents
source_issues.evidence: Receiving systems cannot verify agent identity or trust level. No Ed25519 certificates, no signed receipts, no behavioral monitoring. Explicitly blocking deployment to production systems requiring identity verification.

signals.topic: IngestionPipeline multi-worker mode silently discards cache writes, causing repeated expensive recomputation
signals.summary: When num_workers > 1, cache entries written inside worker processes are never merged back into the parent pipeline cache. Subsequent runs re-execute cached transformations (including costly embedding steps), and pipeline.persist() omits worker-created entries.
aliases: pipeline.run() cache not shared with workers
signals.review_reason: Confirmed bug with identified root cause. Silently wastes compute by re-running cached embedding transformations across pipeline runs. Direct cost impact (extra API calls) and observable performance degradation in any parallel ingestion workload.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: IngestionPipeline with `num_workers > 1` silently loses all cache writes
source_issues.evidence: Root cause identified: self.cache passed to workers mutates in-process copies that are discarded on exit. Affects SimpleKVStore in-memory cache. Causes re-execution of expensive transformations (embedding) on subsequent runs.

signals.topic: BasicMCPClient.get_prompt() crashes on spec-compliant MCP ContentBlock types, blocking MCP server integration
signals.summary: BasicMCPClient.get_prompt() raises NotImplementedError for EmbeddedResource and ValueError for AudioContent/ResourceLink — all spec-valid MCP ContentBlock variants. Any MCP server returning these types causes the prompt retrieval to fail entirely.
signals.review_reason: Confirmed bug — crashes on spec-compliant MCP server responses. The failure is at a core integration point (get_prompt), making the MCP integration entirely unusable for any server that emits non-text/image content. Blocks the primary workflow of calling MCP tools.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: `BasicMCPClient.get_prompt()` fails on valid MCP `ContentBlock` types
source_issues.evidence: Only TextContent and ImageContent are handled. EmbeddedResource raises NotImplementedError; AudioContent and ResourceLink raise ValueError. Breaks any MCP server that returns these spec-valid types.

signals.topic: ReActAgent frequently ignores RAG tools and generates direct LLM responses instead, breaking the agentic QA workflow
signals.summary: Users with workflow-based ReActAgent using multiple CitationQueryEngine RAG tools report the agent regularly bypasses tool calls and produces direct LLM answers, leading to low-quality or hallucinated responses with no citations. The agent also tends to call only one tool repeatedly.
aliases: agent generates direct answers without RAG
signals.review_reason: Despite being labeled 'question', this describes a clear workflow failure: the core agent loop (call tools → get citations → answer) is broken. When the agent skips tool calls, users get ungrounded responses instead of RAG-backed answers — the primary value proposition of the system is negated. Blocking for any production RAG pipeline built on ReActAgent.

source_issues.title: [Question]: ReActAgent Not Consistently Using Tools & Only Calling One Tool
source_issues.evidence: User reports agent often ignores all tools and generates direct LLM responses, even when prompt instructs tool use. Also calls only one tool repeatedly instead of leveraging the full tool suite. Affects CitationQueryEngine-based RAG tools which require tool invocation for citation support.

signals.topic: pip install llama-index times out and hangs during dependency resolution
signals.summary: Multiple users report that pip install times out when installing llama-index packages, particularly with poetry. The installation process takes an abnormally long time and eventually fails, preventing library usage entirely.
signals.review_reason: Installation failure is a complete blocker — users cannot use the library at all. Though reported as a single issue, installation timeouts are a high-visibility first-experience failure that prevents onboarding. Likely caused by oversized dependency graph or heavy transitive deps, which is a legitimate user pain point even at count=1.

source_issues.title: [Question]: Problem pip installing
source_issues.evidence: User reports pip install for llama-index taking very long and timing out, specific to llama-index libraries, using poetry. Other packages install normally.

signals.topic: ruvector CLI commands check for pgvector extension instead of ruvector, causing init/migrate/benchmark/optimize to fail on the official ruvector-postgres Docker image
signals.summary: ruflo ruvector subcommands (init, migrate, status, benchmark, optimize) hardcode checks for pgvector (CREATE EXTENSION vector) but the official ruvector-postgres Docker image ships the ruvector extension. init fails, migrate fails with 'relation does not exist', benchmark fails with 'type vector does not exist', and the -d short flag is also not parsed for benchmark/optimize.
signals.review_reason: 核心设置/使用流程阻断：用户使用官方ruvector-postgres Docker镜像时，init/migrate/benchmark/optimize全部失败。count=3达到高频，官方推荐组合无法工作。

source_issues.title: ruvector init fails: checks for pgvector instead of ruvector extension, blocks migrate
source_issues.evidence: ruflo ruvector init with ruvector-postgres container running: 'pgvector not installed, attempting to create... Failed to create pgvector extension [ERROR] Please install pgvector manually'; ruvector 0.3.0 is confirmed installed via SQL query; migrate then fails with 'relation claude_flow.migrations does not exist'.

source_issues.title: ruvector CLI subcommands hardcode pgvector instead of detecting ruvector extension
source_issues.evidence: status reports 'pgvector extension not installed' even though ruvector 0.3.0 is installed; benchmark fails with 'ERROR: type vector does not exist'; optimize also likely affected. SQL evidence shows ruvector extension present and data healthy (129 entries, 8 tables, 21 HNSW indexes).

source_issues.title: ruvector benchmark/optimize: -d short flag not parsed, requires --database
source_issues.evidence: ruflo ruvector benchmark -d claude_flow fails with 'Database name is required'; --database long flag works; same issue for optimize subcommand; other ruvector subcommands (init, status, migrate) correctly accept -d.

signals.topic: Intelligence hooks cause indefinite hang on every CLI interaction, making the CLI unusable inside ruflo-initialized projects
signals.summary: session-restore and session-end hooks call intelligence.init() and intelligence.consolidate() which synchronously compute PageRank on 150MB of JSON data (18K nodes, 1.3M edges), causing every Claude Code CLI interaction to hang indefinitely (killed at 18-35s, never completes) and the SessionEnd hook to fail 100% of the time. The same CLI works fine outside the project directory.
signals.review_reason: 主流程完全阻断：每个在ruflo项目中的Claude Code CLI交互都无限挂起，必须手动Ctrl+C终止。同一用户在同一机器上验证，14s内无响应，session-end hook 100%失败。虽然count=2未达3，但影响极其严重（CLI完全不可用），review_reason给出强证据。

source_issues.title: [BUG] Intelligence hooks cause indefinite hang — PageRank on 150MB JSON blocks every CLI interaction
source_issues.evidence: CLI hangs indefinitely on every interaction inside project: time claude --print 'hello' inside project = hung at 18s+ killed with Ctrl+C; session-end hook fails 100% of the time with 'Hook cancelled'; intelligence.init() + consolidate() never completed even after 35s when manually killed. 94GB RAM, 24 cores machine — not resource-constrained.

source_issues.title: Hooks causing ~20s latency on every Claude Code CLI interaction
source_issues.evidence: Same user reports ~18-21s per prompt inside ruflo project vs 4.8s outside; session-end hook consistently fails; root cause traced to same intelligence hook system with 10+ hooks across 9 lifecycle events.

signals.topic: Auto-memory hook silently drops all session data due to cross-package import failure; MCP server memory database fails to initialize, blocking the primary MCP use case
signals.summary: AgentDBBackend cross-package import fails silently in hook subprocess, degrading to in-memory Map. Also, when ruflo runs as MCP server via Claude Desktop, the memory database never initializes, causing memory_store to fail with 'Database not initialized' even after CLI init succeeds. Both issues cause persistent memory features to be completely non-functional.
signals.review_reason: 数据丢失（所有session数据静默丢弃）+ 主流程阻断（Claude Desktop MCP模式下memory功能完全不可用）。两issue独立报告同一后果：memory持久化功能完全失效。用户无法利用广告的上下文优化能力。

source_issues.title: fix: auto-memory hook silently drops all session data + 4 packaging bugs
source_issues.evidence: createBackend() instantiates AgentDBBackend which does import('@claude-flow/agentdb') that fails silently; backend degrades to in-memory Map, all data writes succeed but are lost on process exit; .rvf file never created. Fix required 8 separate patches.

source_issues.title: MCP Server: Memory database not initializing - memory_store fails with 'Database not initialized'
source_issues.evidence: ruflo v3.5.51 on macOS Apple Silicon: MCP server starts successfully but memory_store fails with 'Database not initialized'; CLI init succeeds but MCP doesn't access it; embeddings_init fails silently; primary deployment mode (Claude Desktop MCP integration) has zero memory functionality. Blocks advertised token optimization use case.

signals.topic: Missing npm package and semver peer dep mismatch block plugin system installation entirely
signals.summary: @claude-flow/ruvector-upstream@^0.1.0 is referenced by plugins but returns E404 on npm. Additionally, plugin packages declare peer deps with '>=3.0.0' ranges but only alpha versions exist on npm, causing semver pre-release mismatch (alpha.1 < 3.0.0). Both issues block installation of @claude-flow/embeddings, plugin-code-intelligence, security, and other plugins.
signals.review_reason: 插件系统安装完全阻断：@claude-flow/ruvector-upstream缺失导致E404，peer dep semver错误导致所有插件安装失败。用户无法安装任何插件，功能扩展被完全封堵。

source_issues.title: @claude-flow/ruvector-upstream not published to npm (E404)
source_issues.evidence: npm install @claude-flow/embeddings @claude-flow/plugin-code-intelligence @claude-flow/security --legacy-peer-deps fails with 'npm error 404 Not Found - @claude-flow/ruvector-upstream is not in this registry'; blocks all plugins that transitively depend on it.

source_issues.title: Plugin peer deps reject alpha versions (semver pre-release mismatch)
source_issues.evidence: npx @claude-flow/cli@latest plugins install --name @claude-flow/plugin-code-intelligence fails with 'npm error ETARGET No matching version found for @claude-flow/embeddings@>=3.0.0'; plugin declares peer dep '>=3.0.0' but only 3.0.0-alpha.1 exists; per npm semver rules alpha.1 < 3.0.0, so range rejects it.

signals.topic: intelligence.cjs generates 194MB graph-state.json due to duplicate store entries, causing O(n^2) edge explosion and cache misses
signals.summary: parseMemoryDir() produces non-unique IDs across projects (4,482 entries collapse to 157 unique). buildEdges() processes all duplicates creating 1.3M edges. Cache-hit check compares deduplicated count against raw length, always misses. Result: 194MB graph-state.json for 157 unique nodes. This is a root cause of the CLI hang issue.
signals.review_reason: 性能严重退化：单一项目产生194MB状态文件，每次session都触发完整重建，是#1531/#1530 CLI挂起的直接根因。数据文件从MB级降到KB级后session恢复才可能完成。

source_issues.title: Bug: intelligence.cjs graph-state.json grows to 194MB due to duplicate store entries
source_issues.evidence: 4482 entries with only 157 unique IDs; buildEdges() creates 1.3M edges from duplicates; cache-hit check nodeCount===store.length always false (157 vs 4482); graph rebuilt on every session; fix result: 194MB -> 79KB, 1,337,498 edges -> 157. Root cause of intelligence init hang.

signals.topic: HTTPS error ignore flag (--ignore-https-errors / AGENT_BROWSER_IGNORE_HTTPS_ERRORS) not working for recording context and CLI
signals.summary: The HTTPS error ignore setting is not properly inherited or applied in two scenarios: (1) Recording context created by `agent-browser record start` does not inherit the setting, causing goto to time out on self-signed HTTPS pages; (2) --ignore-https-errors CLI flag returns ERR_SSL_PROTOCOL_ERROR on local dev servers. Together these block local development verification with self-signed certs.
signals.review_reason: Blocks headless visual verification and CLI usage for the extremely common local development pattern of self-signed HTTPS certs (mkcert, portless, etc.). Two independent issues both affecting HTTPS error ignore functionality. ProofShot explicitly depends on this feature.

source_issues.title: Recording context does not inherit --ignore-https-errors / AGENT_BROWSER_IGNORE_HTTPS_ERRORS
source_issues.evidence: When AGENT_BROWSER_IGNORE_HTTPS_ERRORS=true, main context works but recording context times out on self-signed HTTPS. ProofShot relies on agent-browser for recording and hits this when verifying local dev servers with mkcert.

source_issues.title: Got 'Navigation failed: net::ERR_SSL_PROTOCOL_ERROR' even with '--ignore-https-errors'
source_issues.evidence: agent-browser open --ignore-https-errors https://my-project.localhost:1355 returns ERR_SSL_PROTOCOL_ERROR despite the flag being set. Blocks local development with self-signed certs served by portless.

signals.topic: v0.24.1 regression: PR_SET_PDEATHSIG kills Chrome after ~7s idle time
signals.summary: v0.24.1 introduced PR_SET_PDEATHSIG in Chrome's pre_exec hook, causing Chrome to be killed after ~7 seconds of idle time on every site. Root cause: PR_SET_PDEATHSIG tracks the spawning thread, not process, so tokio's thread recycling sends SIGKILL to Chrome even though the daemon is still alive.
aliases: Chrome killed by tokio thread recycling
signals.review_reason: P0 regression in v0.24.1 that kills every Chrome session after ~7s of idle time. Clearly demonstrable by user with before/after version comparison. Affects all users who open a page and wait for any period, completely breaking production automation, CI, and any workflow requiring page interaction after a short delay.

source_issues.title: fix: PR_SET_PDEATHSIG kills Chrome in tokio multi-threaded runtime (v0.24.1 regression)
source_issues.evidence: Chrome dies ~7s after open on every page/site in v0.24.1. Reproduces reliably: open page, sleep 10s, get url returns about:blank (Chrome was SIGKILL'd and auto-relaunched). This is a v0.24.1 regression — v0.24.0 works fine.

signals.topic: CDP target lost after SPA form submission — tab becomes about:blank, breaking login/auth flows
signals.summary: After submitting a login form (email/password → Enter or button click), the active CDP target switches to about:blank and all subsequent commands operate on a dead page. The actual page has navigated but agent-browser does not follow the navigation, causing all post-login interactions to fail.
aliases: CDP target switch after form submit
tab becomes about:blank on SPA navigation
post-login commands fail on dead page
signals.review_reason: Directly blocks the most common production automation flow: login/authentication. After any form submission in an SPA, the CDP target becomes about:blank making all subsequent commands operate on a dead page. This means no post-login actions (snapshot, screenshot, eval, navigation) work at all, completely breaking authenticated browser automation.

source_issues.title: CDP target lost after form submission / SPA navigation — tab becomes about:blank
source_issues.evidence: After form submission, tab list shows [0] - about:blank, snapshot returns (empty page), eval runs in about:blank context, screenshot produces blank image. Session cookies from login are lost. This breaks every SPA login flow and all downstream authenticated actions.

signals.topic: AGENT_BROWSER_DEFAULT_TIMEOUT env var not honoured — tests hang indefinitely
signals.summary: When AGENT_BROWSER_DEFAULT_TIMEOUT is set, the CLI ignores it and waits indefinitely instead of timing out. Users expect wait commands to fail fast when selectors are not present, but instead they hang for a very long time and then return a daemon exception.
signals.review_reason: AGENT_BROWSER_DEFAULT_TIMEOUT is a documented configuration meant to control wait behavior, but it is completely ignored. Tests hang indefinitely instead of failing fast, breaking CI pipelines and any automated testing workflow that relies on timeout-based assertions.

source_issues.title: AGENT_BROWSER_DEFAULT_TIMEOUT not honoured in the cli
source_issues.evidence: With AGENT_BROWSER_DEFAULT_TIMEOUT=1000, agent-browser wait '#definitely-not-present' did not fail after 1000ms but waited indefinitely and then returned a daemon exception. Users need proper timeout to validate if pages are working — hanging breaks CI pipelines and automated testing.

signals.topic: Session state persistence (cookies/localStorage) not restored on Linux across restarts
signals.summary: On Linux, both --session-name auto-save/restore and explicit state save/load flows fail to restore cookies and localStorage. The saved JSON contains the expected data but the next launch still starts with empty state. This breaks session persistence for production automation.
signals.review_reason: Session persistence is a core feature for production automation — the saved state JSON is confirmed to contain the right data but is not restored on Linux. Users who rely on persistent sessions (auth state, shopping carts, etc.) cannot use the tool effectively on Linux.

source_issues.title: Linux v0.24.1: state save/--state and --session-name write state but do not restore cookies or localStorage
source_issues.evidence: On Ubuntu Linux x86_64 with v0.24.1, saved state JSON contains correct cookie and localStorage entries, but the next launch restores neither. This is not an empty-file issue — the file contains valid data. Breaks --session-name auto-restore and --state file-based restore.

signals.topic: react-best-practices skill docs provide incorrect code patterns that cause Next.js Server Component runtime errors
signals.summary: The bundle-defer-third-party and bundle-dynamic-imports rules in react-best-practices recommend `ssr: false` with `next/dynamic` inside Server Components, which Next.js explicitly prohibits at runtime. Additionally, the skill recommends compound/dot-notation component patterns that are incompatible with React Server Components. Users following these documented patterns will encounter blocking runtime errors in Next.js App Router projects.
signals.review_reason: Two separate issues confirm that react-best-practices skill documentation contains incorrect code examples for core Next.js patterns. Following the documented bundle-defer-third-party and bundle-dynamic-imports rules causes explicit Next.js runtime errors ('ssr: false is not allowed with next/dynamic in Server Components'). This directly blocks users' primary workflow of building Next.js App Router applications with the recommended skill patterns.

source_issues.title: react-best-practices: ssr: false used without 'use client' in bundle-defer-third-party and bundle-dynamic-imports
source_issues.evidence: Rule docs show `ssr: false` with `next/dynamic` in a Server Component context (RootLayout), which Next.js explicitly throws 'ssr: false is not allowed with next/dynamic in Server Components' at runtime. Users following the documented example will encounter a blocking runtime error.

source_issues.title: Compound Pattern and RSCs
source_issues.evidence: react-best-practices skill recommends compound component dot-notation patterns (Things.A, Things.B) that are not supported in React Server Components. Users following this pattern in RSC contexts will hit build/runtime failures.

signals.topic: Uploading custom skills as .zip fails with 'SKILL.md description cannot contain XML tags' error, blocking skill publishing workflow
signals.summary: Users attempting to upload a custom skill package (.zip file) to the Claude skills section encounter a blocking error: 'SKILL.md description cannot contain XML tags'. This prevents users from publishing or sharing custom skills entirely, blocking the core use case of the platform.
signals.review_reason: Direct user evidence shows the skill upload workflow is completely blocked for custom skill creators. The error prevents users from publishing custom skills to the platform, which is the core platform capability. Though single occurrence, the impact is severe (full workflow block) and affects the platform's primary value proposition.

source_issues.title: Upload Fails with 'SKILL.md description cannot contain XML tags' Error
source_issues.evidence: User explicitly reports being unable to upload a custom skill package (react-view-transitions.zip) due to 'SKILL.md description cannot contain XML tags' error. The upload workflow is completely blocked for custom skill creators.

signals.topic: AI Gateway 503 errors have no automatic retry despite `isRetryable: true` flag
signals.summary: When Google Gemini 3 Flash returns 503 during capacity issues, the Gateway makes exactly one attempt and immediately returns the error, even though the response contains `isRetryable: true`. Users experience complete service failures during provider outages with no automatic recovery.
aliases: no automatic retry on transient errors
signals.review_reason: Main flow failure during provider outages — users get complete service unavailability. The Gateway knows the error is retryable but doesn't act on it, and no fallback is triggered. This is a production-blocking workflow runtime failure.

source_issues.title: AI Gateway: Google Gemini 3 Flash returns 503 with no automatic fallback
source_issues.evidence: Gateway makes a single attempt and returns immediately on 503 even when `isRetryable: true`. `fallbacksAvailable: []` even though fallback config exists. Complete failure during provider outages.

signals.topic: AI Gateway silently falls back from Bedrock BYOK, routing to empty region and bypassing user's AWS credentials
signals.summary: When AI Gateway attempts Bedrock BYOK routing, the constructed endpoint URL contains an empty region (`bedrock-runtime..amazonaws.com`), causing a DNS failure. The Gateway silently falls back to the Anthropic direct API, so BYOK credentials are never used and all traffic goes through system credentials with added latency per request.
signals.review_reason: Silent failure where user's BYOK credentials are completely bypassed on every request. Every Anthropic model request incurs a failed Bedrock DNS lookup before falling back silently. Users cannot leverage their own AWS Bedrock pricing/quotas as intended, with no application-level error to detect the issue.

source_issues.title: AI Gateway BYOK Bedrock routing fails with empty region in endpoint URL
source_issues.evidence: DNS error: ENOTFOUND bedrock-runtime..amazonaws.com on every Anthropic model request via Bedrock BYOK. BYOK credentials never actually used — silent fallback to Anthropic direct API. Added latency per request from failed Bedrock attempt.

signals.topic: Empty reasoning blocks dropped by AI SDK causing Bedrock API validation errors in multi-turn tool calls
signals.summary: The AI SDK strips empty `"text": ""` blocks that appear between reasoning content blocks in Bedrock responses. This corrupts the content block indices sent in subsequent multi-turn requests, causing Bedrock to reject the conversation with a validation error: 'The model cannot modify thinking or redacted_thinking blocks in assistant messages. These blocks must remain as they were in the original response.' This breaks all multi-turn workflows using reasoning models on Bedrock.
aliases: empty text blocks stripped from Bedrock responses
reasoning block index mismatch causes API errors
signals.review_reason: Multi-turn conversations with reasoning-enabled Bedrock models are completely broken. Every multi-step conversation where the model uses reasoning will fail at step 2+ because content indices are misaligned. This is a core workflow failure for Bedrock reasoning model users.

source_issues.title: AI SDK drops "" reasoning blocks but these MUST be included for validation
source_issues.evidence: Empty text blocks between reasoning blocks are stripped, shifting content indices in subsequent API calls. Bedrock API explicitly rejects modified thinking blocks. Error: 'The model cannot modify thinking or redacted_thinking blocks in assistant messages.' Breaks multi-turn tool call flows on Bedrock.

signals.topic: Dynamic tool activation via `prepareStep` invalidates provider prompt cache, causing significant cost increase
signals.summary: When `ToolLoopAgent` uses `prepareStep` to dynamically change `activeTools` between steps, the entire provider prompt cache is invalidated because the tool list in the API request changes. Even though the system prompt and message history are identical, the changing tool array structure busts caching on providers like Anthropic. This negates the cost benefits of dynamic tool activation and makes the intended pattern significantly more expensive.
aliases: prompt cache invalidated by dynamic activeTools
signals.review_reason: Direct cost impact — the intended dynamic tool activation pattern (a documented feature) becomes significantly more expensive due to cache invalidation on every tool activation change. Users implementing tool deferral systems cannot achieve expected cost benefits.

source_issues.title: `ToolLoopAgent.prepareStep` activeTools changes bust provider prompt cache
source_issues.evidence: Dynamic activeTools returned by prepareStep changes the tool list in every API request, busting prompt cache. System prompt and messages stay identical but cache is invalidated. Tool deferral pattern (core use case) becomes significantly more expensive due to this side effect.

signals.topic: `toolChoice: 'required'` constraint is ignored — model skips tool calls despite setting
signals.summary: When `toolChoice: 'required'` is set, the model still does not call any tools on certain turns. This means the core contract of the API — that tools must be called when required — is violated. The user's agent workflow fails because the model bypasses the tool call constraint.
signals.review_reason: Core API contract violation — when a user explicitly requests `toolChoice: 'required'`, the model is still bypassing tool calls. This breaks agentic workflows that depend on reliable tool execution. While only one report, the behavior fundamentally undermines the API's stated guarantees.

source_issues.title: Despite using toolChoice: 'required', ai can sometimes not call any tool during a turn.
source_issues.evidence: User sets toolChoice: 'required' but model still skips tool calls on every turn. Agent workflow is broken because the constraint is not enforced. Affects OpenRouter models via AI SDK.

signals.topic: Turbopack dev: React.lazy with complex hook trees causes infinite Suspense remount cycle, freezing the page
signals.summary: When a component loaded via React.lazy inside Suspense uses 15+ useSyncExternalStore selectors (e.g., Zustand), Turbopack dev mode enters an infinite unmount/remount cycle that freezes the page entirely. The component never becomes interactive. Webpack dev and production builds are unaffected. Only Turbopack (default in Next.js 16) is affected.
signals.review_reason: Dev workflow is completely blocked — the page never becomes interactive. While both source issues are closed as 'invalid link', the body of each contains detailed reproduction steps, a public reproduction repo, console evidence, and a mount-ID tracking analysis proving unmount/remount (not re-render). The workaround (eager import in dev) confirms real user impact. Affects all apps using Zustand/MobX with complex hook trees under Turbopack dev, a common pattern in Next.js 16.

source_issues.title: [Turbopack] Infinite Suspense remount cycle with React.lazy() + 15+ useSyncExternalStore selectors
source_issues.evidence: Component with 15+ Zustand useSyncExternalStore selectors enters infinite unmount/remount cycle in Turbopack dev mode. Each mount gets a new React instance (different useRef value). The page never becomes interactive. next dev --webpack works perfectly. next build && next start works perfectly. Reproduction repo provided.

source_issues.title: [Turbopack] Infinite Suspense remount cycle with React.lazy() + complex hook trees (15+ useSyncExternalStore)
source_issues.evidence: Same issue with Next.js 16.2.1. Mount ID tracking confirms unmount/remount (not re-render). Stub test isolates the problem. 3+ comments confirming. Note: closed as invalid link but reproduction steps and evidence are present in body.

signals.topic: App Router route group prefetch cache entries not isolated by parallel slot, causing incorrect back/forward navigation restore
signals.summary: Route prefetch/cache entries in the App Router can be shared across different route groups/parallel slots that share the same URL-derived key. During browser back/forward navigation, the router may restore the wrong route tree for a parallel slot, causing incorrect page state. The issue was identified and a fix (adding parallelSlot to RouteCacheKey) was prepared in a linked PR.
aliases: back forward cache wrong route tree
signals.review_reason: Back/forward navigation in the App Router can restore incorrect page state for apps using route groups and parallel slots. While non-blocking, this corrupts user navigation history and can cause silent data inconsistency. The linked fix branch (#92335) confirms this is a real bug with an architectural root cause (parallelSlot not in cache key).

source_issues.title: App Router: route groups prefetch cache should isolate parallel slots
source_issues.evidence: Route cache entries shared across route-group / parallel-slot contexts. Cache lookup can collide across entries that share the same URL-derived key but belong to different parallel route slots/route groups. PR/fix branch linked.

source_issues.title: App Router: route groups can share prefetch cache key and affect back/forward restore
source_issues.evidence: Cache entries cross route-group boundaries during back/forward navigation, leading to stale or incorrect restoration. Note: closed as invalid link but the linked correction branch in #92335 confirms the bug was real and worth tracking.

signals.topic: Turbopack: RSC flight client crashes with enqueueModel error during client-side navigation with concurrent triggers
signals.summary: The React Flight client in react-server-dom-turbopack crashes with 'TypeError: chunk.reason.enqueueModel is not a function' during client-side navigation when any concurrent activity (server redirect(), React state updates via SSE/EventSource, or history.replaceState) occurs while the RSC stream is being processed. Once triggered, the flight client is permanently corrupted until page reload. Related issue reported in payloadcms/payload#14860.
aliases: enqueueModel is not a function turbopack
signals.review_reason: Production blocking: RSC client-side navigation completely breaks for any app that uses EventSource/SSE, server redirects, or history.replaceState — all extremely common patterns. Once corrupted, ALL subsequent navigations fail silently until page reload, making the app unusable in production. Despite 'invalid link' label, the issue body contains a full stack trace, a public reproduction, and related confirmed reports in payloadcms/payload#14860.

source_issues.title: Turbopack: RSC flight client crashes with enqueueModel error during client-side navigation when concurrent activity occurs
source_issues.evidence: TypeError: chunk.reason.enqueueModel is not a function crashes flight client during client-side navigation. Three confirmed triggers: redirect() in server components, React state updates via EventSource/SSE, and history.replaceState during RSC processing. Once corrupted, all subsequent navigations fail until full page reload. Production-deployed app with RSC flight. Related: payloadcms/payload#14860 reports identical crash on Next.js 16.0.7 + Turbopack. Note: closed as invalid link but full stack trace, reproduction steps, and workaround commits provided.

signals.topic: Turbopack: WASM fetch URLs return 404 on Vercel due to double-encoded deployment suffix
signals.summary: In Next.js 16.2.0-16.2.2, Turbopack double-encodes WASM chunk paths when deployed to Vercel, causing WASM files to return 404. The deployment suffix (?dpl=) is encoded into the path as %3Fdpl%3D by the first step, then appended as a query param, then the second step encodes it again, resulting in requests for non-existent paths. WASM loading works fine locally. Affected versions: 16.2.0, 16.2.1, 16.2.2. Works in 16.1.7.
signals.review_reason: WASM-based features are completely non-functional in production deployments on Vercel for any Next.js 16.2.x app. The bug has a clear root cause (double encoding of deployment suffix in Turbopack WASM fetch path), is reproducible with a live deployment URL, and represents a regression from 16.1.7. Affects all apps using WebAssembly via Turbopack on Vercel.

source_issues.title: Turbopack: WASM fetch URLs return 404 on Vercel due to double-encoded deployment suffix
source_issues.evidence: WASM files return 404 on Vercel deployment. Root cause identified: Turbopack runtime encodes deployment suffix into path (foo.wasm?dpl=xxx), then N() function encodes each path segment again (encoding ? to %3F), then appends suffix a second time. JS and CSS don't hit this because they load via script/link tags, not fetch(). Works in 16.1.7, broken in 16.2.0+. Live deployment provided: vercelwasm.vercel.app. Reproduction repo provided.

signals.topic: Custom pageExtensions config silently breaks instrumentation.ts — instrumentation never runs or runs with wrong runtime
signals.summary: When a custom pageExtensions config is set in next.config, instrumentation.ts is silently ignored entirely. Even when a proxy file is added to trigger execution, the NEXT_RUNTIME environment variable is incorrectly set to 'edge' instead of 'nodejs', causing instrumentation to run in the wrong runtime. This breaks critical features like OpenTelemetry tracing, database connections, and other Node.js-specific initialization that production deployments depend on.
signals.review_reason: Instrumentation.ts is a critical production feature for observability (OpenTelemetry, Sentry, custom metrics). When broken, entire production monitoring pipelines silently fail with no errors surfaced to developers. The dual bug (silent ignore + wrong runtime) means teams lose critical production telemetry without any indication something is wrong. Standalone Docker deployments are directly affected.

source_issues.title: Custom `nextConfig.pageExtensions` breaks `instrumentation.ts`
source_issues.evidence: With custom pageExtensions (e.g., ['tsx', 'ts', 'universal.ts', 'universal.tsx']), instrumentation.universal.ts is silently ignored unless a matching proxy.universal.ts is present. Even when executed via proxy, NEXT_RUNTIME=edge instead of nodejs. Standard instrumentation.ts (default extension) correctly reports nodejs. Docker standalone deployment. Reproduction repo provided.

signals.topic: createProject API breaking change: secret env var type removed without warning
signals.summary: vercel.projects.createProject 方法悄然移除了对 'secret' 类型环境变量的支持，导致用户现有代码在无任何警告的情况下中断。文档也未标注该变更及类型差异说明。
aliases: secret env vars removed from createProject
signals.review_reason: 该 issue 描述了明确的主流程阻断场景：用户现有代码在无警告的情况下因 API breaking change 而中断。'secret' 类型环境变量支持的移除直接影响项目创建流程，属于关键功能不可用。issue 提供了截图证据证明 createProject 调用失败，有明确用户影响。虽然 count=1 无法达到 P0 阈值，但作为阻断性 regression 应为 P1。排除安全公告、纯功能请求或维护事项，该主题确属用户痛点。

source_issues.title: [BREAKING CHANGE|DOC ISSUE]: vercel.projects.createProject no longer support secret vars so it breaks current code
source_issues.evidence: Issue reports existing production code breaks silently because createProject no longer accepts 'secret' type env vars. No deprecation warning or migration path provided. Documentation lacks any mention of the removed option and does not explain the differences between system/secret/encrypted/plain/sensitive types.

signals.topic: Dirty .gitignore causes node_modules to leak into task input hashes, permanently breaking remote/local cache (v2.8.18+ regression)
signals.summary: Since v2.8.18, any uncommitted modification to .gitignore causes turbo to stop respecting its patterns during task input hashing, leaking node_modules/ into task inputs and busting the cache on every run.
signals.review_reason: 明确的主流程阻断：dirty .gitignore导致缓存完全失效，每次运行都触发重新构建，大型monorepo下性能损失严重。虽然只有1条issue，但提供了完整可复现的regression证据，v2.8.17正常，v2.8.18+回归，影响所有使用.gitignore工作流的用户。

source_issues.title: Dirty .gitignore causes gitignored files to leak into task input hashes (v2.8.18+)
source_issues.evidence: Reproducer shows node_modules/.bin/foo leaks into inputs only when .gitignore is dirty (uncommitted). Cache permanently broken while .gitignore is dirty. In large monorepos, turbo walks hundreds of thousands of files on every invocation. Modifying .gitignore before committing is a normal workflow that silently breaks all caching until committed.

signals.topic: turbo prune --docker injects ~700 phantom npm packages into bun.lock, breaking bun install --frozen-lockfile (v2.8.16 regression)
signals.summary: Since v2.8.16, turbo prune --docker corrupts bun.lock by injecting phantom npm-internal package entries (cacache, libnpm*, @sigstore/*, etc.) that do not exist in the source lockfile, causing bun install --frozen-lockfile to fail in Docker builds.
signals.review_reason: 清晰的回归缺陷：v2.8.16引入，v2.8.15正常，直接阻断Docker prune + bun monorepo的CI/CD流程。Phantom entries数量明确（~700条），修复前需降级至2.8.15，对使用bun的Docker用户造成完全阻断。

source_issues.title: turbo prune --docker injects phantom npm packages into bun.lock (v2.8.16 regression from #12228)
source_issues.evidence: v2.8.16 adds ~700 phantom entries (npm internals like @npmcli/*, @sigstore/*, cacache, libnpm*) to the pruned bun.lock that are not in the source. bun install --frozen-lockfile correctly rejects structural mismatch. v2.8.15 works. Regression from PR #12228. Complete blocker for Docker prune workflows with bun workspaces.

signals.topic: Tasks randomly skipped with no explanation when running from subdirectory or daemon mode (non-deterministic task graph)
signals.summary: Running turbo from a subdirectory or with daemon mode causes tasks to be randomly skipped: turbo reports only 1 package in scope when there should be 15, runs non-existent tasks, and suppresses all output. The behavior is non-deterministic across consecutive runs.
signals.review_reason: 核心构建流程的非确定性失败：任务数量从15随机降至1，运行了不存在的task，远程缓存结果不一致。无任何错误提示，用户完全无感知直到发现构建产物缺失。影响构建正确性，属于P1级别的主流程问题。

source_issues.title: Tasks getting skipped with no explanation
source_issues.evidence: Consecutive turbo runs from subdirectory produce non-deterministic results: one run executes all 15 tasks correctly, the next only finds 1 package. Turbo runs a task (@riptech/app1#tsc) that does not exist in package.json. Remote caching produces different outputs. No error or warning is shown. Primary strategy timeout triggers fallback strategy that causes incorrect package scoping. Affects any monorepo where users run turbo from a subdirectory.

signals.topic: Remote cache misses for binary files across different platforms/environments due to inconsistent hash computation
signals.summary: Binary files (.png, .tgz, etc.) produce different hashes on different platforms/environments, causing remote cache misses even when files are byte-for-byte identical. This defeats the primary value proposition of remote caching.
aliases: binary file hash mismatch remote cache
signals.review_reason: 影响远程缓存核心功能的正确性：二进制文件的跨平台哈希不一致导致缓存完全失效。CI环境中每次都需要重新构建含有二进制资源的项目，浪费计算资源且破坏缓存的核心价值主张。属于P1级别的关键功能不可用。

source_issues.title: [turborepo] Remote cache misses due to different hashes for binary files on different build environments
source_issues.evidence: Identical binary files (png, tgz) produce different hashes on different systems. JS and text files hash correctly cross-platform. This causes complete remote cache misses for any build containing binary assets, forcing full rebuilds on every environment. Directly undermines the core remote caching feature for binary-heavy projects.

signals.topic: turbo prune produces different file hashes for files with CRLF line endings, causing cache misses
signals.summary: After running turbo prune, files with CRLF line endings (on systems with gitattributes configured) produce different hashes than before pruning, causing unnecessary cache misses.
signals.review_reason: 明确的缓存问题但影响范围有限：CRLF文件的prune后哈希变化导致缓存miss，影响使用.gitattributes配置CRLF的Windows项目或跨平台项目。提供完整reproducer，issue本身证据充分，但影响路径相对特定（需同时满足：prune + CRLF + gitattributes），归为P2。

source_issues.title: Pruning results in different hashes for files with CRLF line endings
source_issues.evidence: File hashes are different before and after running turbo prune for files with CRLF line endings. Reproduction repo provided. May be related to .gitattributes not being respected during pruning. Affects any project using CRLF line endings (common on Windows and in gitattributes-configured repos).

source_issues.title: Zed crashes when Cmd+Enter in git hunk
source_issues.evidence: macOS 上 Zed v0.230.1 触发 SIGABRT (Abort trap: 6)；Apple crash report 确认由 main thread 触发；应用完全退出，无错误恢复路径

signals.topic: GitHub Copilot OAuth 认证每 2 分钟失效，用户被迫反复重新登录
signals.summary: GitHub Copilot 提供商模式下，OAuth token 每约 2 分钟失效，AI assistant 无法正常使用，用户需反复登录，完全阻断 Copilot AI 功能。
signals.review_reason: 认证流程反复失败直接阻断 Copilot AI 功能：OAuth token 每 2 分钟失效，用户必须反复重新登录才能继续使用 AI assistant，这是持续性认证失败而非一次性问题，GitHub 账户有充足配额证明问题出在 Zed 端的 token 管理。

source_issues.title: Github Co-pilot OAuth issue, prompting me re-login every 2 mins
source_issues.evidence: 用户在 Copilot 模式下每 2 分钟收到重新登录提示；已确认 GitHub 账户有充足配额；AI assistant 频繁中断，用户体验严重受损

signals.topic: Native devcontainer PR 导致 appPort 数组格式支持被破坏（功能退化）
signals.summary: Zed 对 devcontainer 的 appPort 数组格式支持在 PR #52338 后被破坏，违反 devcontainer 规范（appPort 支持 integer、string、array），用户无法在 devcontainer 配置中使用端口数组。
signals.review_reason: 功能退化直接阻断 devcontainer 多端口使用场景：PR #52338 移除了 appPort 数组格式支持，违反官方 devcontainer 规范。用户在配置包含多个端口的 devcontainer 时功能不可用，是明确的开发环境集成阻断问题。

source_issues.title: Native devcontainer PR breaks appPort array
source_issues.evidence: PR #52338 引入的功能退化；appPort 数组是 devcontainer 规范支持的格式（integer/string/array）；用户无法启动多端口的 devcontainer 配置

signals.topic: Flatpak 版本 Linux shell 环境导入在更新后失败，终端无法启动
signals.summary: Zed Flatpak 版本更新后停止从主机 shell 导入环境变量，改为从沙箱 /bin/sh 初始化，导致用户配置的 shell（如 fish）无法启动，终端功能完全不可用。
aliases: Flatpak shell environment broken after update
Flatpak terminal fails to spawn fish
sandbox shell env instead of host shell
signals.review_reason: 平台级功能完全不可用（终端启动失败）：Flatpak 版本的 shell 环境导入在更新后完全失效，用户配置的 shell（fish）无法启动，集成终端功能阻断。用户已提供更新前后的日志对比，证实这是回归问题，影响所有 Linux Flatpak 用户。

source_issues.title: Flatpak build on Linux stops importing host shell env after update and tries to spawn terminal shell inside sandbox
source_issues.evidence: 更新后 Zed 从 /bin/sh 而非主机 shell（/usr/bin/fish）初始化环境；终端启动失败：Failed to spawn command 'fish': No such file or directory；该问题在更新前正常工作；用户已提供 Flatpak 日志对比证明回归
